title: Flow review duplicates: complete same-run evidence per pair and scoped consumer rewiring (review v2 slices 3-4 subset)
description: Owner ask 2026-09-17: the evidence-based review (including evidence from earlier versions, eneo-ve7i) must also find duplicated work and prepare the improvement. Astra design (session eneo-review-cross-version-design iteration 2, max, green 8). Verified in source on tidy 50849fe8e: ai_builder_flow_review_suggestions.py ~:566 admits duplicated_work with one cited source from any named step and no common run (test_ai_builder_flow_review_suggestions.py ~:185 accepts step 1 output plus step 2 instruction); ReviewEditScope (ai_builder_flow_review.py ~:737, effect guard ~:874) lets only named steps change, so a fold cannot rewire consumers; investigation excerpts are filtered to named steps (~:646). Design: (1) evidence contracts per kind: duplicated_work = both steps' instructions, actual inputs and complete outputs from the same completed run (quotes stay highlights, re-validated at investigation); repeated_prompt_pattern = shared wording alone, never upgraded to duplicated work, and the same prompt on different inputs is not foldable; redundant_context = recorded inputs show repeated material, and a proposal must name the exact material and how every affected consumer keeps its obligations (covers eneo-b7j part c). (2) Separate read scope from edit scope: producers may change; affected consumers get only the server-derived reference/binding substitutions the fold needs, enforced before compilation and on the resulting diff; validate the whole compiled definition (dangling references, changed implicit-source selection, contracts, output obligations). (3) Observation vs actionable decided on the server: mismatched or added consumers make the finding observation-only with the reason shown; the model never grants itself edit authority. (4) Pack complete groups under review_request_budget through eneo-8hn's fitting owner; insufficient budget withholds the actionable claim; caps and one review call unchanged. (5) Historical groups are enabled in eneo-ve7i's activation slice; 'verified improvement' only after eneo-4x2 immutable candidate execution plus eneo-d99 verdicts. Allowed backend files: ai_builder_flow_review.py, ai_builder_flow_review_sample.py, ai_builder_flow_review_suggestions.py, ai_builder_service.py, ai_builder_edit_proposal.py; step_lineage.py and existing compiler/validation helpers only where required. Tests: genuine duplicate folded with consumer rewired and required output preserved; same prompt on different inputs gives no fold; changed or added consumer refuses the actionable suggestion but keeps a justified observation; incomplete, mixed-run, failed-only or lineage-less groups cannot authorize a fold; unrelated consumer prompt/configuration edits refused; implicit, prompt and template references correct after removal and renumbering; one provider-backed discovery check (validator acceptance is not discovery evidence). Do not build: a generic optimizer, similarity index, automatic removal from matching prompts, another graph/rewriter or replay engine, per-model heuristics, larger budgets to force evidence through, token-saving claims for zero-token renderers or reorganized per-item calls.

title: Truncated structured results are accepted as successful outside flows
description:
Astra, session capacity-refusal-necessity it3 (P1, source-verified): non-streaming keeps finish_reason, but CompletionService returns the completion without checking it (completion_service.py:976; adapter:413, :1574). Assistants, apps and services accept the text. Schema parsing validates content, not completeness: valid JSON with finish_reason length still passes (services/service_runner.py:83). Streaming also executes tool calls after a length stop, because the streaming loop does not retain the terminal reason (adapter:2136), while the non-streaming loop already guards it (adapter:1383).

Smallest fix per Astra: preserve terminal reasons through streaming; one shared truncation check when accepting a structured result (explicit response_format or an existing schema-output consumer); typed incomplete-output failure on length; streaming marks delivered content incomplete and ends in a terminal failure; plain text keeps the notice behaviour; the flow guard keeps its current outward error.

Scope: shared model layer - owner approval needed before implementation (see flows scope rule). Related: eneo-8nv2, eneo-jg0x (flow truncation guard).

description: Raised by the eneo-npo gate (2026-09-06). title: Stream flow-step completions so proxy idle timeouts cannot cut long generations
description: Run 23307d61 (2026-09-15 13:43 CEST, flow f96e8648) step 2 failed flow_provider_unavailable after 125.7 s: HAProxy in front of https://gpu.sundsvall.se returned its 504 page (timeout server ~2 min) while vLLM completed at 13:45:31 with 200 OK. Non-streaming completion sends nothing for the whole generation, so every inactivity timeout on the path (HAProxy client/server, any NAT) is a hard ceiling on answer length. Infra mitigation: timeout server/client 900s on that HAProxy. Durable fix: flow-step completions stream through the same provider-call owner the Builder already uses (silence-bounded deadline, see ai-builder-streaming-silence-deadline-20260911), so a token flows every few hundred ms; keep the step deadline as the only Eneo-side ceiling. Also confirm litellm.Timeout from a proxy 504 maps to provider_unavailable retryable=True (it did here). Evidence: worker log 11:45:30Z error_type=Timeout, exception body '504 Gateway Time-out The server didn't respond in time.'

comments.text:
2026-09-16 21:15 Astra orchestration review 3 (score 7) ranks this FIRST by ROI (strongest documented failure evidence), then capacity, then immutable draft execution (eneo-9os), hygiene, test cases (eneo-427). Design constraints, verified in source by Claude:
- Flow steps call the provider with an observer and stream=False; completion_service.py:730 raises when stream and an observer are combined; provider_call_observer.py:177 hardcodes "stream": False in request evidence; the adapter's _observed_provider_call (tenant_model_adapter.py:1564) owns started/completed/unknown receipts.

Preserve provider-reported usage, outcome-unknown on interruption, cancellation, the shared step deadline, and reject truncated streams. Never expose partial streamed text as a completed step. Update the request evidence stream flag.
- Streaming reduces silence during generation only; it cannot help if the proxy times out during queueing, prefill or buffering before the first token.
- Before ranking it above capacity, check whether the HAProxy 900 s mitigation recorded above was deployed and take one correlated long-call trace; if the mitigation is live, urgency drops.
ORDER on the step-execution path: streaming -> P1a snapshot reader -> runtime capacity packaging (1c), serialized, each rebased on the stable preceding interface. Streaming may run in parallel with Builder budgeting (1b) when write sets stay separate.

title: Step-focused edit must not scale its context with flow size (40+ steps)
description: Owner 2026-09-14 14:30: editing one step of a 40-step flow must not overwhelm the model. The eneo-z5u projection sends the target in full, its producer contracts, its consumer requirements, and ONE orientation list of every other step (number, name, mode). Producers and consumers are bounded by the graph, but the orientation list grows linearly with the flow, and consumer requirements can too on a fan-out step. Proposed shape to MEASURE before adopting (memory: deleting context has changed planner quality before, 52 vs 58 on the attachment cohort): keep producers and consumers in full; give names only for a bounded window around the target plus any step the target's own instructions reference; replace the rest with a count sentence ('Flödet har 40 steg, du ändrar steg 17'). Acceptance: input tokens flat as step count grows, no drop in successful target repairs or downstream validity on paired edit runs over a 10-step and a 40-step flow. Needs a large-flow fixture, which does not exist yet.
close_reason: LANDED on tidy ab2b6469f (commit 1be747b7d, owner ruling 08:10 'do the cost issue'): unrelated steps are listed as {step_number, name}; producers and consumers keep their contracts; flow.step_count added. Measured (round 2 receipt): prompt tokens per unrelated step 62/77 -> 20/25 (Luna/gemma), -9.2%/-13.9% at 30 steps, 36/36 first pass, reference-by-name edit resolves 6/6. DECISION recorded, not built: a flat projection (bounded window + count sentence) would also drop names outside the window and lose reference-based edits, the capability Astra reproduced on 5d427fb81; a message-based reference parser is the token-rule class the program deleted in 2.1-S. Residual cost is one short entry per step (about 20-25 tokens); revisit only if 100+ step flows appear. Gate step-context-index-gate green 8 after 5 passes (1: measurement, 2: instruction values, 3: ledger values, 4: lane collision + integration diagnosis, 5: green). comments.text: DESIGN 2026-09-14 14:48 (Astra xhigh, session step-focus-scope-design-20260914, changes_required 6, artifact /Users/ccimen/eneo/flows-tidy-ai-builder/.codex/artifacts/codex-peer-loop-eneo-341-step-focus-context-scope-20260914T123534Z-53456cd9f5de4d1793884ebc8b33600b.md). ANSWER to the owner's hypothesis: previous + current + next is INSUFFICIENT. Use the target's DIRECT producers and consumers (one hop is the right default: for A->B->C, changing A leaves B's declared output and C's declared input unchanged, and full-flow validation checks every edge), plus complete server-side validation of the merged flow; do NOT send a transitive closure. Delete the positional window entirely: include names and numbers alongside actual dependencies plus a flow-count sentence. Per-mode context: renderer = actual body source, input/output types and delivery config (a renderer does NOT inherently consume the whole flow); template fill = exact bindings, template identity and control metadata, required scalar paths and types; review checkpoint = target policy, reviewed output contract, relevant producer policy; form/runtime input = referenced fields with types/requiredness/constraints, all applicable fields for whole-input reads. TWO DEFECTS Claude missed, both reproduced by local probe: (P1) an incompatible IMPLICIT JSON consumer passes both authoring checks (producer's required output changed summary -> different while its previous_step JSON consumer still requires summary; validate_spec and _validate_saved_step_consumers both pass, only runtime input validation fails; flow_validators.py:798 returns immediately for previous_step) so the downstream safety this slice claims is incomplete for implicit chaining; (P2 of the pair) the dependency projection misses runtime aliases and whole-input reads ('{{ föregående_steg }}' projects no producer, '{{ flow_input }}' with a declared form field projects no form fields; ai_builder_flow_context.py:105). (P2) Deleting the orientation list CANNOT deliver flat cost on its own: the scoped tool schema still requires the complete ordered list and enumerates every permitted keep reference, and repairs replay previous tool arguments, so untouched steps still cost input tokens, output tokens and repair context. ORDERED SLICES: (1) dependency and contract correctness (ai_builder_flow_context.py, shared reference analysis, flow_validators.py; adjacent template_reference_analyzer.py, ai_builder_validation_references.py, ai_builder_edit_proposal.py) - complete alias/whole-input projection, reject incompatible implicit JSON chains before a proposal is approvable; (2) remove the model's unchanged-step round trip (edit_tool_schema, plan_edit_context, edit_proposal, edit_compiler, request preparation) - admit ONE target modification, server-expand, compile and validate, identities/order/revision checks intact; (3) reduce orientation context WITH measurement, degree-aware not 'flat with flow size'; (4) user recovery and publication copy (typed-failure change SEPARATE from the UI copy/entry change). Next: slice 1 to an Astra worker.

title: Flow editor autosave drops edits made during an in-flight save and self-collides with stale_revision
description: Reported 2026-09-15 by a colleague: while selecting 5-6 items in the flow editor the toast 'Flödet ändrades av en annan användare. Dina ändringar beräknas mot den nya versionen.' fires repeatedly and only one of the six selections survives; the colleague asked for a classic Save button. Root cause (tidy 9340dc05f, same on dev image 88e3d1e): (1) FlowEditor.scheduleAutoSave fires editor.saveChanges() 500 ms after every change with no in-flight guard, so a second full PATCH /flows/{id} is sent while the first is still running; (2) PATCH /flows/{id} carries no expected_revision, FlowRepository.update fences on the draft_revision read at request start, so the second request of the same user hits the fence and gets 400 stale_revision with the 'another user' text; (3) ResourceEditor.saveChanges snapshots update at save start and, for a full save, replaces update with the server response on completion (applyUpdates field=undefined returns the server copy), so every edit made during the flight is discarded even when no conflict occurs. Fix at the owner (ResourceEditor, shared by Flow/Assistant/App/GroupChat/SpaceSettings editors): serialize saves (one in flight, coalesce later changes into one follow-up save), and merge the server response three-way so fields edited during the flight keep the local value and are saved next; FlowEditor re-points _temp_ step ids to the real ids by assistant_id after each save (it already does this for the active step only). Server: PATCH /flows/{id} should accept expected_revision from the editor so the fence reflects what the editor saw, and the stale_revision message must not claim 'another user' when the caller collided with itself. Keep autosave; a Save button would keep the same clobber on the explicit save path (FlowEditor.flushFlowSaves uses the same saveChanges). Tests: ResourceEditor concurrent-save ordering and three-way merge; FlowEditor.test.ts 'classifies each overlapping save' must be revisited since overlapping saves no longer happen.

title: Edit approval carries the pre-preparation diff, not the plan the user approves
description:
Found by the Codex commit gate (session review-suggestions-gate, iteration 21, 2026-09-06) while gating the review-edit scope. Pre-existing and NOT specific to review turns: it affects every AI Builder edit.

In ai_builder_edit_proposal.process_edit_arguments, compile_edit_proposal produces both the compiled spec and an approval whose FlowEditDiff describes that compiled spec. prepare_compiled_spec_for_session then runs (ai_builder_compiled_spec_preparation.py:49), which disambiguates duplicate step names and canonicalizes resources, and its output replaces the spec. The approval is then copied forward with the ORIGINAL diff and returned beside the final spec. So the diff the user is shown can describe a plan that is not the plan they are approving. test_ai_builder_compiled_spec_preparation.py:390 proves preparation renames the second of two duplicate-named steps.

Codex's smallest safe correction: derive the effective diff from the current flow and the final prepared spec, and place that same diff in the approval; keep the authored-proposal check for model feedback. current_flow_authoring_spec() builds the baseline and _build_step_changes() (ai_builder_edit_compiler.py:587) computes the changes, so the pieces exist; _build_step_changes would need to become public.

What is already closed on review turns (commit for slice 2b): validate_review_edit_effect holds the COMPILED diff to the review scope, and review_edit_renamed_outside_the_scope refuses a preparation-time rename of a step the findings do not name. Those bound the review path; they do not fix the disclosure defect for ordinary edits.

Acceptance: the FlowEditDiff in the approval describes the spec actually returned, with a test that makes preparation rename a step and asserts the approval reports it.

title: Dictated JSON input: no input_contract is emitted when the user describes the payload without a schema
description:
Evidence (advanced_explicit legs, 2026-09-06): advanced_explicit_open_eplatform_mapping and advanced_explicit_integration_validation both dictate an incoming JSON contract ("Inkommande payload och utgående resultat ska ha separata kontrakt", "Flödet tar emot JSON från en kommunal integration"). The compiled plan has the right step (input_source flow_input, input_type json) but its input_contract is None in 3/3 observations on both the parent and the candidate arm, so the harness check expected_input_contract_schema fails and the runtime validates nothing.

Cause: _apply_flow_input_schema only fills input_contract from a resolved declared input schema (SchemaEvidence). When the user describes the payload without pasting a schema, nothing is emitted.

Decision needed before implementing: what a truthful contract is when the payload's fields are unknown. Options include a permissive object contract, a contract derived from the fields the user did name, or asking one discovery question. Inventing field names is not acceptable.

description: Owner ask 2026-09-15: Granska med AI-byggaren should make a working-but-badly-built flow (example: IBIC package, 14 steps) more token- and step-efficient, fold duplicated steps and split oversized ones, without losing detail or quality, verified on previous runs. title: Honor explicit step inputs in frontend type-chain validation
description:
Problem: imported flows that explicitly project JSON from an earlier step are incorrectly rejected when the immediately preceding step outputs PDF. Backend has_explicit_underlag already gives bindings precedence; frontend getFlowStepValidationIssues does not. Owner: existing flowStepTypes validation and flowUnderlag binding inspection. Scope: align frontend chain checks with explicit question/source_refs semantics, regression tests for earlier JSON sources and absent/empty bindings, preserve actual implicit-chain errors and global rules. No backend/runtime, model prompts, schema, or data changes. Acceptance: exported IBIC package validates unchanged; explicit JSON source_refs work after PDF and with all_previous_steps; empty bindings keep implicit validation. Verify nearest flow validation tests, frontend typecheck/lint and repository hooks. Risk: over-skipping checks for invalid bindings; retain separate binding validation. Recovery: revert focused code commit. User authorizes commit and push to refactor/flows-tidy-ai-builder.

## Steps to Reproduce
Import a flow whose final text writer has JSON input and source_refs projecting fields from an earlier JSON step, while the immediately preceding step renders PDF. The editor reports typed_io_incompatible_type_chain and marks JSON as legacy-invalid although the selected underlag supplies JSON.

## Acceptance Criteria
Use existing getFlowStepUnderlag to align implicit-chain checks and input-type options with explicit bindings. Keep first-step/global constraints and implicit PDF-to-JSON rejection. Prove the old failure then pass nearest binding, type, config, template and transition tests; pass frontend typecheck/lint and commit hooks. Push the focused fix to refactor/flows-tidy-ai-builder without modifying unrelated work.

title: Investigation planner reliability: batch per suggestion or measure the planner's evidence capacity
description: From the eneo-a89 measurement (2026-09-06, gpt-5.6-luna, 922k window): review-backed proposals carrying 28k+ tokens of run excerpts (3-6 suggestions, 24-28 excerpts) failed 4/4 with schema rejections after repair, while 12-16k tokens (single suggestion) passed 2/2; the suggestions call handles 61k tokens fine. Mitigation landed: review_investigation_evidence_max_tokens (default 16000, admin-changeable, null removes) bounds the excerpts' share of the proposal prompt. Long-term options to weigh: (a) investigate one suggestion per proposal turn and merge (Undersök alla becomes a batch of scoped edits), (b) carry only the cited sources per suggestion plus the named steps' instructions, (c) a planner capacity measurement per model that derives the bound from capability instead of a shipped number. Measure with the cohort legs and the owner's flow before choosing.

title: Direct-compose reports render 'Extraktionsvarningar: []' on every clean source section
description: Found in the owner-ordered line-by-line re-judgement of the landed D worker output (05c5d9781). The direct-composition item template written by document_report/topology._compose_source_record_item_template always contains the line 'Extraktionsvarningar: {extraction_warnings}' (or 'Extraction warnings: ...'), and the runtime renderer _render_source_ref_value / _source_ref_value_to_text (runtime/step_input_resolution.py) renders list values via json.dumps, so a clean source (empty warnings list) renders 'Extraktionsvarningar: []' in the final report and a degraded one renders the raw JSON list of codes. The compiler test asserts the template string, not a rendered section. Fix (Claude): the item renderer drops a template line whose placeholders all rendered empty, an empty list renders as nothing, and a list of strings renders as a comma-separated list; tests for the renderer and one rendered per-source section with and without a warning. Ownership: runtime/step_input_resolution.py (renderer) + tests; the topology template stays.

title: Upstream LiteLLM: reasoning_effort mapping must keep the thinking budget below max_tokens or reject explicitly
description: Found 2026-09-17 in slice B of eneo-nb0 (LiteLLM 1.101.0). AnthropicConfig maps reasoning_effort for non-adaptive models to thinking.budget_tokens (litellm/llms/anthropic/chat/transformation.py ~:1594) without clamping to max_tokens, so requests with a cap at or below the mapped budget (captured: cap 512 or 4096 -> budget 4096) are rejected by Anthropic. The SDK's cap_thinking_budget_to_max_tokens (~:1290) is not called on that path, and calling it alone is not enough because it drops thinking when the cap is below the minimum budget. Eneo's decided behaviour (Astra ruling) is to send the bounded cap and the selected effort unchanged and surface the provider rejection. Upstream fix should keep both controls valid when possible or raise an explicit error; after it ships, bump the pinned LiteLLM version and re-run the reasoning tests. No local SDK patch.

title: Probe: knowledge retrieval ProviderRejectedRequestException on 3 of 8 IBIC section steps
description: Owner run 34768545 (2026-09-21 21:41, package 1.0.1, Gemma-4-31B on vLLM, run completed 17/17 in 546 s). Steps 9, 10, 11 (Personlig vard, Hemliv, Relationer) report knowledge_retrieval status=error, retrieval_error_type=ProviderRejectedRequestException, error_code=rag_retrieval_failed, 150-200 ms, unique_sources 0; steps 5-8 and 12 with the same knowledge configuration retrieved 2 sources each. ProviderRejectedRequestException is raised by litellm_transport.py:249 on a BadRequestError (HTTP 400) from the embedding provider. Query owner: derive_rag_retrieval_query (step_execution_runtime.py:159) bounds the query to RAG_RETRIEVAL_QUERY_CHAR_LIMIT=2048 CHARACTERS (step description + input excerpt); the embedding model bounds in TOKENS. description: Follow-up to eneo-e82 (do after it). Astra design pass 2026-09-13 (session flow-review-evidence-20260913) + Claude's read of the pipeline. title: Limit the two-limit capacity refusal to flows and the AI Builder; chat, assistants and apps keep their old behaviour when a model lacks a limit
description:
Owner decision 2026-09-17 16:55 (answer to Claude's scope report): limit it to flows.

Facts (Claude-verified on tidy 5752cf29d):
- 880f8f0f3 made TenantModelAdapter._prepare_dispatch_kwargs (completion_models/infrastructure/adapters/tenant_model_adapter.py:1167) run on every dispatch (call sites :1631, :1767, :2229, :2627, :2707).
- It calls ModelCapacity.resolve_output_cap (completion_models/domain/model_capacity.py:66), which requires both max_input_tokens and max_output_tokens and raises UnknownModelCapacityError otherwise. Streaming maps that to a 422 error event (:2787).
- So chat, assistants and apps on any tenant model missing either limit are refused, not only flows.
- The lab runs 50849fe, which predates 880f8f0f3.

Must land BEFORE the lab deploys a tidy build that contains 880f8f0f3.

Scope: this is an owner-approved change to the shared model adapter (exception to the flows-only rule). Flows and the AI Builder keep the strict rule (unknown stays unknown, typed refusals). Every other caller dispatches as before 880f8f0f3 when a limit is missing.

Astra designs and gates it. Keep the caller-side distinction explicit, not a silent fallback for flows. Planned for the next session.

title: Vemsa: closed failure kind on job status; whisper request timeout follows the audio duration
description:
Repository: eneo-ai/vemsa (standalone; no board there, tracked here). Problem (verified 2026-09-20): (1) JobStatusResponse (api/jobs.py:31-38) exposes 'error' as free text only, and JobOutcome keeps error_class for stats; a consumer cannot tell a bad input from a capacity failure (OOM after VEMSA_OOM_MAX_ATTEMPTS, jobs/queue.py:545) or a provider outage, so Eneo maps every failure to 'invalid request, not retryable'. (2) pipeline/whisper_api.py:80 sends the whole file in ONE whisper request under a fixed VEMSA_WHISPER_TIMEOUT_S=3600 while VEMSA_MAX_AUDIO_BYTES admits 2 GiB; a multi-hour recording on a busy GPU exceeds the fixed timeout and fails as a provider error although the audio was fine. audio_duration is already measured in pipeline/transcribe.py:117.

Deliverable: (a) add failure_kind: Literal['input','capacity','provider','internal'] | None to JobStatusResponse, derived where the worker records the failure (queue.py, the same place error_class is set); keep 'error' as the human text; document the closed set in README 'Job API'. (b) the whisper request timeout is derived from the measured duration (a per-request client timeout: fixed connect/read floor plus a bounded multiple of audio seconds), replacing the fixed default for transcription; VEMSA_WHISPER_TIMEOUT_S becomes the floor. (c) expose updated_at on the status response (already on Job) so a consumer can see a job is alive. Optional; only if the Eneo bead's design pass picks liveness-based waiting.

Non-goals: chunked transcription; webhook changes; queue limit changes (100 global / 10 per client stay; Eneo waits on 429). Acceptance: tests for each failure kind on the status endpoint; a timeout test proving the derived timeout scales with duration and never drops below the floor; README updated. Pair: eneo-yhsy (Eneo consumer side).

title: Flow drift check misses a changed model route: execution snapshot ignores the model name that tenant routes are built from
description: Found by the Astra failed-run recovery design (2026-09-17) and verified in source on tidy 50849fe8e: flows/assistant_execution_snapshot._completion_model_execution_surface hashes only the model id and litellm_model_name, but tenant models store litellm_model_name = None (tenant_model_service ~:269, route built at runtime from provider_type + name) and allow renaming name (~:342, moves the route). TenantModelAdapter dispatches model.get_model_route(provider_type) (~:524). So an admin who changes a tenant model's name to another provider model keeps the same execution surface hash, the executor's drift check passes, and published flows silently run a different model, against the owner's no-silent-model-switch rule. Fix at the canonical snapshot owner: include the actual resolved route and execution-affecting settings in the execution identity (display names excluded); old evidence that cannot establish identity is classified honestly (for recovery: ineligible). Shared prerequisite for failed-run recovery (eneo-3e4) and P1a (eneo-9os). Model agnostic.

title: Stale RUNNING detection should not wait for the 4 h invocation ceiling
description: Since eneo-zjdh, TASK_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS defaults to 14400 and the stale-run reconciler (runtime/tasks.py _reconcile_stale_running_runs_all_tenants, flow_run_recovery_policy.flow_stale_running_reconcile_after_seconds) derives its threshold from it, so a run whose worker died stays RUNNING for over four hours before reconciliation, and the health policy reports it unhealthy only after the same window. Design: detect liveness from the attempt's heartbeat/lease (the executor already records progress; add a periodic attempt heartbeat or use the ARQ job liveness) so a dead worker is reconciled within minutes while a live 3 h step is left alone. One owner for staleness; the ceiling stays the budget, not the liveness signal. Needs an Astra design pass (persistence + reconciler semantics).
close_reason: Landed on tidy e4970d9ed and pushed (5 lane commits rebased onto 5baffa96d): execution_heartbeat_at on FlowRuns initialised atomically with the claim and renewed by one loop per execution worker fenced on the run revision; ownership loss cancels the invocation and its provider work; every execution publication (results, transcript words, checkpoints, delivery intents, generated and overflow files) is fenced under the parent-run lock and rolls back on loss, while a late result after recovery still reports the run's honest terminal outcome; recovery locks the parent run before judging expiry and pending delivery, discovers expired heartbeats through a dedicated index under a global budget with a finite sweep window, and terminalizes through the existing terminalizer with typed recovery facts; health reports on the same signal; reversible idempotent migration 202609201200 with cutover and the rolling-deployment rule documented. Recovery is now about 3-4 minutes after the last renewal instead of the 4 h ceiling. Evidence: three gate passes (max; the third held only for execution evidence), 555/560 full integration with the 5 failures fixed by the late-result correction, focused re-run of the five affected files 53 passed, unit suites green except the 4 known OpenAPI failures (DX-1 fixes them), migration_isolation retry cases green, bare pyright 2 pre-existing, svelte-check 0 errors, schema regenerated. title: Flow retries lose the step's uploaded runtime input files since the rerun cut
description: Found while restoring the integration baseline (eneo-xg2, 2026-09-07). FlowRunRepository.create writes flow_run_step_input_files for attempt_no=1 only; the rerun and retention cut (fb8231158) removed copy_step_input_files_from_predecessor_attempt and no other writer exists. The executor reads input files per attempt (_list_step_input_file_ids(attempt_no=attempt_no)), so a step retried as attempt 2+ with runtime input enabled would resolve zero uploaded files. Either retries must carry attempt 1's files (one owner in create_or_get_attempt_started or the activation input) or input files must be keyed per step, not per attempt. test_flow_run_listing_and_evidence_measurement_contract encodes the old expectation (a step result at attempt 3 lists the run's input files) and is the one integration test left failing on purpose; fix it with the product decision.

title: Failure card: surface the server's actionable validation problem and its matching action instead of generic invalid-proposal copy
description: Follow-up to eneo-lq7 from the owner's first browser look 2026-09-13: for self_correction_invalid_plan the card says 'Planen höll inte måttet den här gången' with 'Förtydliga uppgiften' as the primary action, while the server knew the specific problem (a template-fill flow needs exactly one selected DOCX template). When the public error's details carry an actionable problem (template attachment selection, a named missing binding, a schema the user dictated), the presentation owner (aiBuilderFailurePresentation.ts) renders that problem as the consequence and offers the matching action (e.g. 'Välj en DOCX-mall' opening the attachment/template selector) as primary; generic copy only when no actionable detail exists. Needs the error contract to expose the problem class in details (not display text), sv/en copy per class, DOM tests per class, presented_as stays the coarse class with the specific problem recorded as a sub-fact if the data model should learn from it.

title: Long recordings lose transcript segments above 256 KiB, so review corrections and word timings fail around three to four hours of diarized speech
description: Found 2026-09-21 09:16 while answering the owner's codec question (Fable). Codec and bitrate change AUDIO size by an order of magnitude (5 h: ~50 MB Opus, ~300 MB MP3 128k, ~3.2 GB 16-bit WAV) but transcript text and diarization sizes track speech duration only. The binding limit for a 4-5 h meeting is NOT the 8 MiB inline text cap (a 5 h transcript is ~1 MiB) and not any audio size; it is MAX_SEGMENTS_BYTES = 256 KiB in runtime/transcription.py:231. Production segments serialize as {file_index, start, end, speaker, text, optional speaker_attribution, overlap_ids} (transcription.py ~:250). ESTIMATE (assumption stated, no receipt yet): text alone is ~63 KB per hour at 150 wpm and 7 bytes per Swedish word; with ~80 bytes of overhead per ~10 s segment the segments array is ~95 KB per hour, so the cap is reached between ~2.7 h (short segments) and ~4.2 h (text-only floor). eneo-hy7c's 5 h measurement records result size and must replace this arithmetic. WHAT HAPPENS above the cap (verified in source at f42e2def9): serialize_segments omits the array with reason too_large (:644-:654, :699); words are omitted because they anchor to stored segments by index (MAX_WORDS_BYTES 8 MiB is not the binding limit); application/flow_transcript_corrections_service.py extract_transcription_segments returns None explicitly for the omitted-for-size case (:52-:73) and the corrections service raises FlowBadRequestException (:163), so review corrections are REFUSED; flow_transcript_regeneration_service.py renders from original segments (:211) so regeneration cannot run either. WHAT SURVIVES: downstream steps read the text (the material reader parses the timestamped lines); speaker-name mapping works because build_speaker_inventory(source_text) reads the text (step_handlers/speaker_mapping.py:121), with its own 8 MiB text check. This is independent of eneo-uwbv (file-backed transcripts above 8 MiB of text, ruled P3 today) and independent of codec. CANDIDATE FIXES, not decided, Astra validation required before a spec: (1) give segments their own row exactly as words already have (FlowStepTranscriptWords pattern) with the same 8 MiB cap, keeping the index anchoring, so the step payload stays small and the edit owners read the row; (2) spill segments to a sibling JSON artifact with an alias, the A2 the uwbv design pass described, now justified by a real need. The 256 KiB guard exists to keep the step's stored input payload small, so the fix must keep that property rather than raise the number. DO NOT build a container format or change the text artifact contract.
close_reason: Both slices landed: 1e56690f5 (immutable transcript-source row per attempt, typed reader, three bounds) and b3f602bee (every reader cut over, embedded 256 KiB cap deleted, paged transcript-source route, UI on the paged loader). Long diarized recordings keep every segment, speaker and word timing; corrections require the source hash; exports carry the rows within the existing budget. Follow-ups: browser check on a lane stack; the 5 h measurement (eneo-hy7c) on the owner's environment.

Reviewers of a long meeting lose anchored text corrections, speaker-review decisions, word timings and regeneration from reviewed text once serialized evidence crosses the cap; the transcript UI explicitly disables editing without stored segments. Text, downstream processing, speaker-name mapping and playback from parsed timestamps survive. Direction: option 1 (segments in their own row) is the better fit, REVISED: copying the words table's replacement semantics would lose historical source evidence, so segments must be preserved per transcription attempt including retries and regenerated-run snapshots. Blockers to resolve in the spec before implementation: attempt-scoped retention; the cutover must include checkpoint propagation, API and UI readers, and evidence exports; the shared segments-and-overlap cap and export memory accounting must be resolved; migration, unavailable-data behavior and behavior tests specified up front. comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Design findings recorded 2026-09-21 10:15 (Astra max, verified claims marked). FINDING THAT CHANGES THE SIZE: the runtime caps the COMBINED segments-plus-speaker_review object and discards segments when overlap metadata alone makes it too large; a read-only execution of the actual cap block discarded a 270,082-byte segment array AND a 102-byte segment array accompanied by oversized review metadata, both losing words. So diarized recordings with overlap detail can lose segments far below the duration estimate; the second trigger must be resolved, not only the array moved. Words are replaced on conflict by run and step and tolerate absence, so 'exactly like words' would give authoritative segments the wrong lifetime: earlier attempts must keep resolving their own evidence. Reader inventory (nine, beyond the three I named): corrections service :115 (source hashes, anchors, speaker edits), regeneration :166 (original segments and word indexes), words service :72 (staleness against current segments), corrections propagation :138 (segments required to approve and continue), checkpoint service :1010 (word-to-text placement), API assembler :216 (recomputes the public source hash), frontend transcriptSegments.ts:173, FlowRunEvidence.svelte:297 and FlowRunReviewCheckpointPanel.svelte:313 (playback and correction state), evidence bundle :602 and attempt export (generic payload forwarding). Regeneration needs a snapshot WRITER: prefix seeding copies input JSON, so a reference would not copy the source row into the child run. Exports must include transcript rows explicitly and measure their logical bytes before hydration. DIRECTION: revised option 1, one immutable transcript-source row per transcription attempt containing segments and associated review detail; words stay an optional derived index; ONE typed transcript-source reader with resolved data passed into pure propagation and projection functions; bounded detail loading for both review surfaces, large arrays kept out of listings. Delete during cutover: embedded segment writes, the 256 KiB omission path, the corrections service's storage extractor. Do not build: a container format, editor-specific readers, per-model limits, a permanent dual-storage fallback, a higher inline cap. LANDING ORDER: slice 1 schema plus typed source-reader foundation; slice 2 one complete producer and consumer cutover across all nine readers. Verification bar: a result above 256 KiB loaded, corrected, approved and regenerated through the real UI and API with small list payloads; overlap-heavy fixture keeps uncertainty details and anchored words; historical evidence resolves after retry; stale correction writes refused; rollback, cancellation and a fenced-out worker leave no reference to missing data; regenerated child independent of parent; exports include the source and refuse oversized loads before hydration; the measured five-hour result fits all three detail budgets. Measurement first: production-serialized bytes for segments, words and overlap metadata separately and together (eneo-hy7c). THREE PRODUCT DECISIONS put to the owner: oversized results complete with an explicit review-unavailable state versus failing a review-required flow (pass recommends the explicit state unless review is mandatory); existing runs with retained segments migrated once, already-omitted segments unrecoverable and users retranscribe (recommended); historical source content and regenerated-run independence preserved by default (recommended).

title: Run create: an idempotent replay returns its run even after a republish
description: Found by the module robustness gate it3 (2026-09-23). FlowRunService.create_run loads the published definition with expected_flow_version (flow_run_service.py ~370) before the idempotency lookup (~611), and the fingerprint includes flow_version. So a client whose create response was lost, replaying the same key after the flow was republished, gets flow_run_stale_version although its run exists; it cannot learn the run's id. Standard idempotency: a replay with a known key and the same request returns the stored run regardless of later state. Owner fix candidate: resolve the key first (key + principal), and when a run exists, compare the fingerprint against the request prepared at the run's pinned version; return it on match, RUN_IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT otherwise; only then apply the published-version check. Module today handles it safely without this (recording sealed from the first send; same-key resend at the current version either creates the run or conflicts to 'already sent'), so this is a QoL/correctness follow-up, not a blocker. Needs its own gate; integration tests for replay-after-republish, conflict, and first-send stale.

title: Capability snapshot: narrow a persisted control on provider refusal evidence
description: Follow-up to the sampling-control retry. The persisted SupportedModelKwargs snapshot is the request-shape authority, but discovery (LiteLLM get_supported_openai_params) marks temperature tunable for GPT-5-class and o-series models that accept only the default, so every Builder call on such a model pays one refused round trip (~2 s) until an admin turns the control off. Design: when a provider refuses a control by name (unsupported_parameter/unsupported_value), persist a narrowed snapshot on the tenant model row with evidence provider_discovered (never widened again), through the tenant model service; the chat adapter and the flow runtime send the same controls and would benefit. Operator workaround today: disable temperature on the model in the tenant model admin (admin_explicit evidence).

comments.author: ccimen
comments.text: Codex design pass 2026-09-11 (gpt-6-astra xhigh, session ai-builder-budget-rule-validation, iteration 13): changes_required, score 6. Blockers before any implementation: (1) POLICY: an unsupported_value refusal of one value (e.g. temperature=0.0) does not establish the control is unsupported; either retain typed observations (parameter, value, code, phase) and only learn from parameter-level evidence, or name conservative suppression as an explicit operational policy (owner decision). (2) Narrowing must target the exact tenant-owned, non-deleted row with a conditional atomic update keyed on the observed model/provider revision (CompletionModelRepository reads include global rows; admin edits can race). (3) tenant_model_service.update refreshes capabilities whenever 'reasoning' is present in the payload, which the admin UI always sends (draft.ts:242): an unrelated admin save would rediscover and restore the refused control; refresh only on a real route/reasoning change. (4) Observation collection must be independent of retry admission and proposal telemetry (review path and budget-denied refusals would be missed); pass one bounded observation collection through Builder calls, persist best-effort once per model after execution. (5) A fourth evidence tag is rejected by current readers, which then resolve ALL optional controls as unsupported: readers must ship before writers (deployment order) or the tag must be avoided. (6) Widening ProviderCapabilityRejectedException.capability requires updating tenant_model_adapter.py:1597 (records every capability rejection as response_format_rejected) and must not activate the runtime's response_format fallback. Design brief: scratchpad design-capability-narrowing.md. Decision needed from the owner on (1) before implementing.

title: Make semantic proposal repair converge without terminal errors
description:
TL;DR: A valid Flow architecture can still terminate during proposal self-correction when a compositional text step fails to consume all relevant structured predecessors. Preserve the critic and make the canonical typed repair path converge generally, without case-, prompt-, filename-, or corpus-keyed behavior.

Problem and evidence

Report-layout R4 candidate C1 produced `self_correction_quality_failure` with typed code `final_text_step_must_reference_relevant_structured_outputs` on an otherwise valid document-to-DOCX-template architecture. Exact parent completed the same control first pass. The same exact candidate completed it first pass in R3, so the failure is provider-plan variance reaching a real fail-closed repair seam, not evidence of a deterministic report-layout transformation defect. R4 stopped before repeats and all 172-case legs. Immutable receipt and verdict identities are recorded on measurement task `eneo-flow-ai-builder-production-readiness-m55.5`.

Why it matters

The user sees a terminal Builder error after answering a valid canonical question. A retry may succeed, but relying on provider luck violates the production no-hard-failure gate. Weakening the critic would allow under-bound plans and is not acceptable.

Current and proposed canonical ownership

The typed invariant remains owned by `ai_builder_critic_invariants.py`. Failure classification remains owned by proposal finalization. Repair convergence should remain in the existing proposal self-correction/retry owner; do not add a second repair service, a case-specific compiler branch, or another prompt-only fallback. First determine whether the correct smallest complete solution is better typed repair feedback, a deterministic owner-level normalization already supported by the plan contract, or deletion/consolidation of a duplicate repair path.

Scope and non-goals

- Reproduce the generic topology class from typed plan contracts, not from the benchmark wording or fixture.
- Inventory preserved receipt incidence for this exact failure code across parent/candidate history and distinguish deterministic source behavior from provider variance.
- Add behavior-first RED proof at the stable proposal finalization/retry boundary.
- Implement only a general canonical-owner correction that preserves compiler, critic, source-evidence, architecture, and no-retry contracts.
- Do not change report-layout questions, corpus, fixtures, expectations, benchmark adjudication, provider model, broad classifier authority, or failure floors.
- Do not weaken or special-case `final_text_step_must_reference_relevant_structured_outputs`.

Acceptance criteria

1. A generic valid architecture with at least two relevant structured producers cannot terminate solely because the repaired compositional step omits one producer; the existing typed repair owner either produces a critic-valid plan within the bounded retry contract or returns an explicit non-retryable cause that is not falsely presented as provider success.
2. Existing invalid plans are still rejected by the critic.
3. DOCX template-fill, generated document, report-layout, form-field, and unrelated simple-flow behavior remain unchanged.
4. No case-, corpus-, prompt-, localized phrase-, file-, or model-ID keyed production logic.
5. Decisive isolated tests, full Builder unit suite, full Flow unit suite, relevant integrations, canonical Pyright, Ruff/format, hooks, and one exact-diff Codex peer gate score at least 8 pass before commit.
6. Any provider-backed remeasurement uses a new integrated candidate, prospective addendum, fresh roots/spaces, ten-minute minimum plus exact-parent health gate, all targeted repetitions, then all six fresh 172-case legs. No landing on any hard, quality, repair, expectation, question, latency, call, or token breach.

Recovery

Keep the report-layout candidate `985aa3f3b3009d22144ad691643101548166fa78` unpushed. If the general repair cannot be proved without broadening ownership or weakening a contract, make no source change and return for an explicit owner decision.
acceptance_criteria: Typed generic repair convergence is proven without weakening critic or adding case-specific logic; deterministic suites and peer gate pass; provider-backed no-regression measurement remains required before landing.
close_reason: Deterministic canonical-owner repair is committed locally and fully gated; provider no-regression evidence remains owned by m55.5.

title: Require report layout before committing multi-source report architecture
description:
TL;DR: Prevent a new multi-source generated-report architecture from being committed before the user-owned report layout is resolved. Reuse the existing aggregation relevance predicate and canonical question catalog, deepen the architecture gate, and delete the duplicate relevance projection. Preserve irrelevant shapes and old prerelease commits.

## Problem and value

Per-source sections, synthesized overview, and both create different deterministic flow topologies. Current code can commit a relevant new architecture with report_disposition absent. Close that gap without broad smartness, phrase matching, defaults, or case-specific behavior.

## Canonical owners and allowed paths

Reuse report_disposition_is_relevant in ai_builder_aggregation_intent.py. Extend ai_builder_architecture_derivation.py for the new create-mode commit gate. Delete the duplicate helper in planning_state_builder.py. Limit behavior tests to existing action-policy, architecture-derivation, degraded-classifier, server-decision-dispatch, service, replay, and integration-session owners. be39ddbd65283e4c8abbf79cabe010a51a778e03 is evidence only; rebuild it on the synchronized baseline.

## Product contract

Require the field only for document input plus generated PDF or DOCX report output plus multiple or flexible document scope. Ask the existing canonical bilingual closed question when unresolved. Do not ask for single-source, non-document, non-report, DOCX template-fill, edit-mode, unknown-prerequisite, already-pending, or applied-plan shapes. Existing pinned commits with a missing value stay pinned; later commit-grade evidence may trigger existing revise_architecture behavior.

## Non-goals

No migration, compatibility reader, reopen or invalidation path, policy default, new service, retry, fallback, classifier compaction, phrase table, prompt-keyed rule, case ID, corpus key, source-count threshold, benchmark edit, or release change.

## Baseline and stopping rule

First merge origin/develop a243cbbe7e onto origin/refactor/flows-tidy-ai-builder a65083bac773 in an isolated worktree with a650 as first parent and record the exact baseline SHA. Build the candidate separately and record its SHA. Never touch BANKED 0.4 paths. No push is authorized. Any deterministic failure, peer score below 8, or frozen measurement-floor breach stops the slice.

## Acceptance Criteria

Exact baseline and candidate SHAs are recorded. New relevant create-mode architectures cannot commit without commit-grade report_disposition. Irrelevant and prerequisite cases remain unchanged. Existing commits with a missing value remain stable; later strong evidence revises through the existing drift owner. The duplicate relevance helper is deleted. Focused provider failure persists the canonical report question without committing. Replay and edit invariants pass. Targeted tests, complete Builder suite, shared boundary suites, complete Flow unit suite, canonical whole-project Pyright, Ruff, formatting, and diff checks are green. title: Keep report topology channels aligned after lowering
description:
TL;DR: A valid multi-source report can terminate before proposal creation when document-report lowering changes a step's predecessor from TEXT to JSON but retains the previously derived input channel. Recompute the server-owned derived channel from final lowered adjacency so all supported report layouts compile without weakening typed validation.

## Problem and impact

R2 produced a hard `architecture_materialization_failed` for an explicit report whose classifier evidence and architecture commit were correct. The report lowerer replaced a weak TEXT section writer with a structured JSON section writer. A following retained JSON overview step still carried `underlag_channel=implicit_previous`, derived against the removed TEXT predecessor; the final JSON-to-TEXT boundary requires `whole_object`. This is a latent general compiler bug exposed by the new architecture gate, not a benchmark-specific miss.

## Ownership

- Current and proposed canonical owner: `ai_builder_assembly/document_report/lowering.py`, which owns the structural rewrite.
- Invariant owner to preserve: `ai_builder_assembly/plan.py::derive_underlag_channel` plus `FlowAssemblyPlan` validation.
- Reuse the existing derivation function after final report adjacency is known. Do not duplicate its rules, weaken validation, or create a generic repair service.

## Smallest complete slice

- Add a provider-neutral compiler behavior test for a reader JSON → weak section TEXT → retained overview JSON → terminal TEXT outline.
- Prove all non-null report dispositions remain valid after lowering, while the exact `both` shape produces the deterministic compose topology.
- Re-derive the server-owned underlag channel for lowered previous-step adjacency at the report-lowering boundary.

## Deliberate non-goals

- No classifier, prompt, question, architecture-gate, provider adapter, harness, corpus, fixture, expectation, runtime execution, UI, migration, or public API change.
- No case ID, phrase, filename, language token, model-output name, or report-specific exception in the typed validator.
- Do not cherry-pick unrelated historical aggregate-contract or extraction-warning candidates.

## Validation

- RED/GREEN focused compiler regression.
- Existing report-disposition compiler matrix and assembly-plan invariants.
- Full Flow AI Builder unit suite, full Flow unit suite, relevant integration tests, canonical Pyright, Ruff, format, diff check, and repository hooks.
- One exact-staged Codex xhigh peer gate before local commit. No push.

## Risk and rollback

Risk is bounded to server-owned report topology projection. Incorrect broad normalization could mask provider defects, so only the derived channel may change and the typed plan validator remains authoritative. Rollback is the single local commit; R2 receipts remain immutable and cannot be rerun under the same addendum.

comments.text: DESIGN 2026-09-14 16:27 (Astra xhigh, session provider-400-diagnosis-20260914, changes_required 7, artifact .codex/artifacts/codex-peer-loop-builder-edit-turn-provider-400-diagnosis-*.md). ROOT CAUSE OF THE INCIDENT: NOT identified, and Astra refused a causal green light without correlated provider evidence. It weakened two of my candidates by synthetic check against the INSTALLED SDK: LiteLLM 1.98.0 converts max_tokens 128000 into max_completion_tokens for Azure GPT-5 (gpt_5_transformation.py:255), so the wrong-parameter-name theory is out; and an ordinary unsupported_value/temperature response DOES survive the installed adapter and our extractor, so the incident carried a different envelope. Still live: the deployment's accepted token-limit VALUE, parallel_tool_calls, the edit schema. ROOT CAUSE OF THE EVIDENCE LOSS: REPRODUCED. provider_error_fields (ai_builder_provider_call.py:227) consults the buffered response only when error.body is not a Mapping; an EMPTY mapping is still a Mapping, so the fallback is skipped and code+param come back null even when the buffered response carries unsupported_value and temperature. MY CLAIMS CORRECTED: another_call_permitted is always false in the final classification (so it does not prove no retry ran); the fingerprint covers only stage/kind/status (so identical fingerprints do not mean identical causes); outcome_kind server_confirm_requirements does not identify the failing turn because the confirmation dispatcher makes no proposal call; unclassified_outgoing_field_count describes SDK input, not wire JSON; the packed figure is fixed_input_tokens 5669. REJECTED from my proposal: bounded provider MESSAGE excerpts, even behind an operator setting (a length limit does not stop prompts or credentials); and giving param the same freedom as code (paths carry user schema names). DECIDED: deepen ONE owner (provider_error_fields) into a typed rejection record with safe code, normalized param, extraction source/status, provider correlation id; delete provider_expectation rather than populate it. Lane fix/ai-builder-provider-rejection-evidence in worktree eneo-ai-builder-provider-evidence, worker impl-eneo-gs0 (astra high), spec at scratchpad/spec-eneo-gs0.md. comments.author: ccimen
comments.text: LOCAL REPRODUCTION 2026-09-14 16:34 (Claude, real openai SDK + httpx.MockTransport against the installed backend venv, scratchpad/probe2.py). Results change the leading hypothesis. (1) An ordinary Azure temperature refusal (error.code=unsupported_value, error.param=temperature) is extracted CLEANLY by provider_error_fields, and identically whether stream=True or stream=False. So streaming is not the differentiator, and the production incident was NOT an ordinary temperature refusal: had it been, safe_detail would have carried provider_parameter=temperature and the 600fb10b1 retry hook would have had its named control. (2) Exactly two envelope shapes lose both facts: an APIM/gateway envelope {statusCode, message} with no error object, and an Azure error object carrying a message but no code and no param. Both produce code=None param=None, which is precisely what the incident logged. (3) Control shapes confirm the parser is otherwise fine: content_filter extracts its code, and an invalid_value/max_completion_tokens rejection extracts both. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE FIX: the mapping-guard defect Astra reproduced is real but is NOT what happened here, because the SDK populates error.body from the same response it buffers, so the two agree. For this incident class the provider sent no machine-readable code at all, so no allowlist or envelope-fallback change can recover it. The ONLY thing that would have identified it is the provider correlation id from the response headers (apim-request-id / x-ms-request-id), which an Azure admin can look up server-side, plus an extraction status saying the provider sent no machine-readable code. That must become the primary requirement of this slice; the envelope fallback stays as secondary hardening. Astra's refusal to log message prose stands and is unaffected.

title: Review fact: a step near its model's capacity (input or output tokens vs ModelCapacity), observation-first with a split/narrow remedy
description: Owner idea 2026-09-19 23:38: the evidence-based review should look at a step's input and output token counts against the model it ran on and suggest splitting (or narrowing its input) when a step is too close to the limit. Today the review has token_share (a step's mean share of the run's tokens, ai_builder_flow_review.py:196-203) but nothing relates a step's tokens to the model's declared limits. Owners to reuse: ModelCapacity (completion_models/domain/model_capacity.py, two limits, unknown stays unknown), receipt-derived per-attempt usage (eneo-4x2 slice 1, prerequisite: rejections contribute nothing, unknown withholds), the resolved model per attempt (requested_model / execution identity eneo-cuty), the review policy for the threshold (never a literal). Proposed: step_near_capacity fact per step over the cohort, input and output judged separately; suggestion kind delivered first as an OBSERVATION with a named remedy (explicit bindings to narrow input, or split), the actionable split handed to whole-flow editing with existing validation/diff because a split adds a step and rewires consumers (eneo-078k owns scoped rewiring later). comments.author: claude
comments.text: Astra design ruling 2026-09-19 (session builder-morning-program-design, max, changes_required MIN 6): DEFERRED behind a measurement contract. (1) Grain: step receipts sum all completion calls of an attempt (mapped items, tool rounds), so utilization must be computed per provider CALL before aggregating; report peak normalized call ratio + affected-run count over measured runs + a witness run/attempt/model + explicit withheld coverage, input and output separately; never a mean that hides saturation. (2) Denominator: persisted provider_call records carry route ids and usage but no declared capacity or dispatched output cap, and declarations are mutable, so a historical pressure claim needs the dispatch metadata recorded through the existing observer/receipt owner (a preceding slice), or the fact is labelled 'against currently declared limits' and makes no historical claim. Reuse ModelCapacity + the adapter's effective-cap semantics (a 60k input against 100k/50k yields a 40k output cap), FlowProviderCallRepository for bounded projection, review_run_admission/review_facts for eligibility and output; one named threshold beside the existing review thresholds, no operator setting. First delivery = a deterministic FACT/observation; no suggestion/action workflow, no automatic splitting, no forecaster, no backfill from live settings.

title: vadsa: serve streaming and batch from one model instance, loaded without a double GPU peak
description: Found 2026-09-26 setting up vadsa on a laptop RTX 3070 (8 GB) next to Vemsa (3.3 GB): startup fails with CUDA OOM inside the FIRST load (PipelineBuilder -> ASRInferenceWrapper.load_model, 3.43 GB allocated). vadsa loads pianissimo-sv twice by design (engine/nemo.py: the buffered streaming pipeline plus a second ASRModel.from_pretrained for batch), each with map_location=cuda, so the checkpoint and the weights are both on the GPU while loading. On an H100 this does not matter; on 8-24 GB municipal GPUs it decides whether vadsa fits next to Vemsa. Investigate: (1) batch transcription through the pipeline's own model (the scheduler already serialises GPU work on one thread; check whether transcribe(timestamps=True) mutates decoding state the streaming pipeline relies on), (2) load to CPU then move. Measure peak and steady VRAM before and after; realtime and batch outputs must stay identical on the fixture set. Workaround today: demo-stack/run-vadsa-review.sh runs vadsa on the CPU (32 s clip: batch 2.2 s; realtime median lag 1.3 s, done 2.1 s after the audio).

comments.author: ccimen
comments.text: 2026-09-26 18:00 Claude: investigated sharing one instance on NeMo 3.0.0 — unsafe as a plain reuse. RNNTModel.transcribe(timestamps=True) (models/rnnt_models.py:292-315) permanently calls change_decoding_strategy(self.cfg.decoding) when compute_timestamps differs, replacing whatever decoding the streaming pipeline configured (greedy_batch, CUDA-graph decoder, per-stream biasing from conf/buffered_tdt.yaml), and _transcribe_on_begin/_on_end toggle further model state. A shared instance would change live decoding after the first batch call. Safer options, in order: (1) keep two instances but load each to CPU first and move to the device, removing the checkpoint+weights double peak (the OOM here happened inside the FIRST load at 3.43 GB); (2) measure bf16 weights for the batch instance against the fixture set; (3) sharing only with an explicit save/restore of the decoding config around batch calls, pinned by a test on the NeMo version. Low priority while the target is the H100.

title: Flow worker deadline cancels execution before timeout can be persisted
description:
## Steps to Reproduce
Run the registered flows.execute coroutine beneath its configured ARQ deadline while execution exceeds TASK_EXECUTION_TIMEOUT_SECONDS. On parent 5ab3b91f both timers expire together; the outer timer cancels execution before the inner timeout owner can persist flow_task_timeout. The asynchronous regression reproduces this without provider calls.

## Acceptance Criteria
The registered worker uses the existing flow_task_hard_timeout_seconds policy (execution budget plus 60 seconds); cancellation precedes timeout persistence; genuine process death still converges through stalled recovery without automatic provider replay. Validate through platform runtime unit tests, real database timeout terminalization, Redis/ARQ process-crash recovery, Ruff and full Pyright.

Canonical owner: backend/src/eneo/worker/platform_tasks.py consumes backend/src/eneo/flows/domain/flow_run_recovery_policy.py. Only worker registration, its regression test, the existing operations runbook and this issue change. No migrations, model calls, flow-package edits or larger execution budget. Revert the commit to restore old behavior; worker rollout is required. The original 50849fe incident is consistent with stale reconciliation but precise causality remains unverified without worker logs and resolved attempt timeout. Default 3600-second budget still spans all steps between review pauses; this is documented separately from the deadline-ordering defect.
close_reason: Implemented and deterministically verified worker deadline ordering using the existing policy owner; timeout persistence and hard-exit recovery tests pass. Not deployed; reported devserver incident causality remains unverified.

title: Abandoned runs are failed after a bounded wait; history is never purged automatically
description: Owner ruling 2026-09-20 15:37: NO automatic purge of flow history, ever (flows can be sensitive, e.g. classification 3; purge only through the explicit settings-driven administrator action, eneo-vxyw). Separately, a run that is started but never finishes (waiting for a review approval that never comes, approved-never-resumed, stuck in a non-terminal state) may be FAILED automatically after a bounded wait so it does not sit open forever; its history stays. comments.text: DESIGN DECIDED 2026-09-20 20:30 (Astra xhigh, session stuck-runs-design, verdict changes_required MIN 6 on my brief; all decisive findings verified in source). State contract: queued+dispatch active -> existing redispatch; queued+dispatch exhausted -> abandoned after the wait anchored to dispatch_pending_since; running+live heartbeat -> continue; running+expired heartbeat, no pending delivery -> flow_worker_stalled; running+pending delivery -> delivery owner; awaiting_review with awaiting/edited checkpoint -> EXISTING expires_at policy (14 d default, max 90 d; run cancelled with flow_review_expired: NOT duplicated); awaiting_review with APPROVED checkpoint -> flow_run_abandoned after the interval from approved_at, checkpoint cancelled with approval facts PRESERVED, no automatic resume; terminal -> untouched. Liveness: execution_heartbeat_at on FlowRuns initialised atomically with mark_running_if_claimable (revision as the ownership fence), one worker renewal loop over its active invocations (30 s renew / 180 s expiry / 60 s sweep), renewal conditioned on run+tenant+revision+running; ownership loss stops the invocation; terminal update rechecks eligibility. Bounded payload-free sweep with a total invocation budget and matching indexes. NO failure webhook promise (no such contract exists). Slices: (1) heartbeat ownership, (2) recovery + health, (3) uncovered waits (approved-unresumed, exhausted queued) with flow_run_abandoned + typed facts, (4) consumer contract docs/examples folded into each. dgh9 = slices 1+2; il5s = slice 3.

title: Flow AI Builder: conversational core v2 - bounded replacement experiment (one interpretation, server requirement record, one action per turn)
description: Owner 2026-09-26 asked whether to rethink instead of improving bad to ok. gpt-6-astra xhigh (builder-rethink-0926 it1, MIN 6 on current architecture; saved demo-stack/specs/builder-rethink-astra.md): EVOLVE via a bounded replacement of the conversational core, earned by a paired experiment; not a wholesale rewrite. Root problem: competing owners of meaning (heuristic readers, classifier, defaults, discovery, critic; server summary prose fed back as user text). Target: one model-owned interpretation, one server-owned requirement record (goal/constraints with evidence, existing typed domain contracts for inputs/outputs/schemas/file roles/runtime fields/checkpoints, revision-bound edit scope, evidence source+quote verified by server, resolution unknown|stated|inherited|policy_default|conflict; explicit answers keep authority; defaults cite policy; assistant wording never becomes user evidence), server-owned gaps (key, path, reason, answer contract; one question at a time), one bounded action per turn. Tools: read_flow(refs) (server picks dependency context) and submit_turn(expected_revision, requirements_delta, action = answer(message) | ask(gap_key, question, options) | propose(NewFlow | ChangeSet) | unsupported(code, affected_refs)); compile/validate automatically after propose; bounded typed conflicts. Edit = change list over the ordered compiler (Modify/Add/Remove/Move, omission preserves, scope independent of operations, delivery+reads, final-spec preservation incl. placeholders). Experiment budget: 3 calls/turn, 8,192 output tokens/call incl reasoning, 32k tokens and 90 s/turn. Experiment: same pinned corrected backend/transport/settings for both arms; 11 create cases + E02,E10,E12,E14,E16,E17,E22,E28,R01 + 4 dialogue probes (explain alternative, material ambiguity, correction, already-supplied info); 3 reps per arm/model/case (<=288 sessions), start with 1 rep, stop early on a hard preservation violation. Continue only if BOTH models: zero collateral mutations/dependency loss; all mechanical and clarification controls pass; >=95% fulfilment separately for create and edit, no case below 2/3; all dialogue probes pass; and >=10 pp fulfilment gain or >=20% fewer Builder tokens per fulfilled request at equal/higher fulfilment; no p95 latency/token regression. Else keep the evolved pipeline and delete the prototype. Migration: per-session implementation; offline shadow first, then flagged create sessions, edits only after applied/executed preservation passes; delete replaced heuristics/classification merge/discovery re-analysis/catalog semantics per migrated path. PAUSE: new phrase readers, question catalogs, discovery layers, classifier retries (eneo-8yh retry/loop-guard deferred). CONTINUE: guards lane, eneo-0hn, C1.1 reader, change-list edit contract (eneo-ofm8), efficiency caps/telemetry/compact projections (eneo-lqg1), edit benchmark (eneo-e7h6). Prerequisites: corrected backend (lane, reader, edit contract) and the edit benchmark lifecycle.

- Package import does not apply the portable config models.

title: Flow AI Builder: measured token and latency reductions (efficiency slice)
description: Owner 2026-09-26: remove wasted and duplicated work so the Builder is fast and token-efficient without losing quality; model-agnostic. Audit: demo-stack/specs/builder-efficiency-audit-20260926.md (132 bundles, 121 classifier captures, in-process timings). Classifier = 77% of gemma tokens / 63% luna; gemma latency ~9.7 ms per completion token vs 0.05 ms per prompt token (output tokens cost seconds). No prompt caching used or recorded. Ranked: (1) classifier output cap - done in eneo-3og9 lane (16,384); (2) record reasoning tokens (dropped at ai_builder_litellm_completion.py:351-371), then A/B the lowest declared reasoning setting for classification only (gemma hides ~2.9k reasoning tokens, ~28 s of a 35.7 s first turn) - ties to the absent-effort 'low' fallback on eneo-8yh; (3) replay asked questions compactly into proposal prompts (id, text, option labels: ~98 vs ~597 tokens) and ensure_ascii=False at planner_request_preparation.py:1314 (+22% from escaped Swedish); (4) short classifier source ids mapped back in the parser (user_message:<uuid> is 22-26% of classifier output, ~150-200 output tokens/call); (5) gate upload-only prompt rules/schema when no files are attached (~470-690 tokens/call); (6) cache the pure text-normalising function in discovery (4.5x faster ask turn, currently blocks the event loop) and build the discovery profile once per turn (built 3x) and the critic context once per edit attempt (2x); (7) stop a repair loop when a repair repeats the identical typed failure (the failed edit repeated one failure 3x, ~15k tokens). Each change: before/after on the frozen cohort both models, quality non-inferior (accepted, questions, output checks), tokens and latency reported.

title: Whether: submit audio to Vemsa by signed original URL instead of streaming the blob through the worker
description:
Status quo (safe): RemoteFlowTranscriber._run_job (remote_transcription.py:694-735) holds file.blob fully in memory, writes it to a temp file, measures duration and uploads it multipart under FLOW_TRANSCRIPTION_SERVICE_SUBMIT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=600. For a 2 GiB recording that is 2 GiB worker RSS plus 2 GiB temp disk per concurrent transcription and a 3.5 MB/s upload floor. Vemsa accepts source_url submissions (fetch with VEMSA_FETCH_TIMEOUT_S=600, bounded by VEMSA_MAX_AUDIO_BYTES) and Eneo already mints signed original-file URLs (files/file_router.py generate_original_signed_url).

Question first (design brief, one pass): is Vemsa able to reach Eneo's API/object store in the deployment? If yes, submitting the signed URL removes the memory spike and the upload timeout coupling with a small diff (mint the URL with an expiry covering the queue wait, send source_url, keep the digest for the receipt from the stored file metadata instead of re-reading the blob). If no, close as decided: the streaming path stays and the memory cost is documented in the no-tune defaults (eneo-ls78). Non-goals: chunked upload, resumable upload. Acceptance if built: a unit test that the blob is never read into memory on the source_url path; the receipt keeps the same identity fields.
close_reason: Folded into eneo-qr0a (yhsy 4): signed-URL submission alone does not remove the memory cost because File.blob is hydrated before either transcriber; the bounded audio path owns the whole question.

title: Whether: durable execution substrate (DBOS Transact on Postgres) instead of the hand-built claim/heartbeat/recovery/dispatch trio
description:
Raised 2026-09-21 from an external recommendation. NOT a change to make now; a question to answer at a planning session, with a decision test that costs nothing extra.

The case for: checkpointed steps, timers, signals for human approval and automatic resume after a crash are exactly the lifecycle holes this program has been closing by hand: dispatch retry ladder, mark_running_if_claimable, execution heartbeat + ownership fence + recovery sweep (eneo-dgh9, landed 2026-09-20), approve-and-continue, retry from a failed step (eneo-3e4), abandoned waits (eneo-il5s), and durable remote waiting (eneo-b7bu). DBOS is a library over Postgres with no extra server, which fits the deployment; Temporal needs a server a municipality would have to run, secure and back up, so it is the weaker candidate here.

The case against, from what actually broke on 2026-09-20: the failures were transaction-semantics problems in OUR schema, not missing retries or timers. Gate findings: the ownership fence missed generated-file publication; recovery evaluated expiry and pending delivery without first holding the parent-run lock (a delivery committing during the lock wait was invisible under READ COMMITTED); the migration held an exclusive DDL lock through a backfill; a late result after recovery hid whether the run was cancelled or failed. A durable engine still makes you write the activity that publishes a result, and it does not know about tenant scoping, revision-as-ownership-token, the audit outbox, review checkpoints with decision actors, or the evidence-gap facts. All of those invariants are currently gate-verified against source; moving substrate means re-proving them in a layer the reviewer cannot read end to end.
Timing: pre-release with deployments imminent is the worst moment to swap the execution substrate, and it would retire code that only just became measured and green.

DECISION TEST (costs nothing extra): build eneo-b7bu (release the execution slot while a remote transcription job runs, resume through the fenced dispatch) BY HAND first. It is the smallest piece a durable engine would own. If that slice is painful and fragile, that is the evidence the substrate is wrong and this question becomes a real epic. If it is straightforward on top of the landed heartbeat and dispatch owners, the engine buys less than it costs and this closes as decided.
Do not evaluate on a toy flow: the evaluation must cover tenancy isolation, one audit row per mutation, revision fencing and the review-checkpoint decision contract.

title: S-D One capacity contract: input limit I and output limit O, no separate context window, unknown stays unknown
description: Astra iteration 1+2 + slice-1 design. Conflict today: tenant_model_adapter.get_token_limit_of_model (~2730) treats max_input_tokens as the INPUT budget; AIBuilderRequestBudget (ai_builder_settings.py:34/85, planner_request_preparation ~705) treats it as the shared window; migration 20260303_split_token_limit_into_input_output assigned custom models max_output_tokens = min(token_limit // 4, 4096) without provenance. Owners: completion_models/domain/completion_model.py (~92), the API model, DB model + migration, tenant adapter, context builder, Builder budgeting.
