title: Builder: a failed force-new session leaves no session and no retry
description: Raised by gate pass 5 on the handoff UI (2026-09-06). FlowAIBuilderDriver.createSession resets the whole driver state (abort, #resetFlowState) before the POST; when the POST rejects it surfaces the error and rethrows with hasSession=false. Every force-new path shares this: the header 'Börja om' (FlowAIBuilder.svelte handleStartOver), BuilderTurnAlert's start-over, and the replace-edit confirmation (which since 1d8a4429b correctly refuses to open the step/review on rejection). The generic error surface (BuilderTurnAlert) offers only dismissal; after dismissal the host shows the no-session skeleton and only a page reload recovers. Owner: the driver's createSession + the host's no-session branch. Fix shape to weigh: keep the current session until the new one arrives (reset after the POST resolves), or on rejection re-run initialize(targetKind)/resume the previous session id, and give the error surface a retry that re-runs the captured launch (review or saved step). Add the test 'force-new fails once, succeeds on retry, reaches the requested destination without remounting'.
close_reason: Landed on refactor/flows-tidy-ai-builder as a8be2d517. createSession keeps what its reset replaced - the state plus the uncertain-turn fence - and puts it back when the create is refused, so every force-new path leaves the user on the session they had instead of the no-session skeleton; the session is published before the draft GET; the refused forced create is recorded against the exact error it installed so the create-mode alert keeps offering the retry while that error stands; the saved-step scope is owned by the session it was opened from; and both surfaces clear their composer context only once the replacement is real, with the header consuming the rejection. Tests (all RED-verified on 50a86976b): FlowAIBuilderDriver.test.ts 'keeps the session it has when a forced new one is refused, and retries onto it', 'keeps the uncertain turn fence when the fresh session is refused', 'keeps the refused start-over offer only while its own error stands'; FlowAIBuilder.dom.test.ts 'keeps offering the fresh session when the first attempt is refused', 'keeps the edit and its step scope when the header start over is refused' (held draft GET), plus the extended 'does not open the review when the replacement session cannot be created'; FlowAIBuilderService.test.ts 'does not lend the saved-step scope to the session that replaced it'. Gate lane-reliability-npo-gate 4 -> 6 -> 7 (3-pass cap); the pass-3 blocker was fixed after the cap and landed as recorded residue with local verification, as the reviewer itself advised. Validation: ai-builder vitest 359 passed, svelte-check 0 errors, eslint/prettier clean, backend untouched. Follow-up: eneo-2jd.

title: Builder edits flows like a coding agent edits files: anchored instruction patches, full-fidelity reading with a budget, one derived authoring reference, attachment roles, per-model measurement

Proposed order: P1 anchored find/replace patches on instructions applied server-side (refuse absent/ambiguous anchors; preserves untouched clauses by construction; shrinks output tokens; supersedes eneo-dfmk); P2 full authoring spec in context when it fits, else a bounded read_step tool; P3 one derived authoring reference generated from the validator's models; P4 attachment roles (process description / input example / output template) settled by one decision-value question, packages always via the importer; P5 per-model measurement with the package-edit probe (backend/scripts/ai_builder_package_edit_probe.py), a create-from-document journey and the battle harness with frozen floors. title: Runaway output abort: fail a completion fast when the stream produces only whitespace (evidence: Gemma NVFP4 on vLLM wrote one fact then 54k tokens of newlines)
description: Evidence 2026-09-21 21:15 from the owner's dev server worker log (run 9e1443d3, step 3 of the IBIC package 1.0.1 with bounded contracts, hosted_vllm/nvidia/Gemma-4-31B-IT-NVFP4): the model emitted one valid fact (F1 in underlag.krav.uppgifter) and then 163,598 characters (~54k tokens) of '\n        ' repeated until finish_reason=length after 626 s; the 913 most common 80-char windows are pure whitespace. No maxItems/maxLength bound can end it because the item never closes; whitespace is legal JSON. This is the whitespace trap of quantized models under grammar-constrained decoding (model/serving side: xgrammar backend or repetition penalty or a non-quantized build fixes it). Eneo's part, per the Astra ruling on eneo-v0ta (conditional slice 3, deferred until evidence): consume the completion stream internally at the observed completion-call boundary (extract the reconstruction/cleanup mechanics from ai_builder_provider_call.py ~:195, keep the complete-response interface), and abort with a typed client-side failure when the output contains no non-whitespace token for N consecutive tokens (N an intent, e.g. 256) after at least one token of content, keeping the partial as rejection evidence, recording unknown final usage honestly (no fabricated zero usage, no completed receipt, no automatic retry), honoring the existing attempt deadline and request hashing. Acceptance: a scripted streaming provider replaying this run's shape fails within seconds with the typed code and retained head; a legitimate long answer with normal whitespace is untouched; the non-streaming path stays for providers that cannot stream. Design brief + Astra validation (xhigh) before a worker.

title: Inline object-content reads hydrate the whole payload; streaming inline audio needs EXTERNAL TOAST storage and a chunked reader
description: Found 2026-09-21 09:25 when the eneo-qr0a worker blocked (correctly) on the spec's claim that a streaming download owner exists for all audio. Verified: object-store audio streams (object_content/s3_object_store.py reads a botocore StreamingBody in chunks), but PostgreSQL-inline audio is selected whole (object_content/content_repository.py ~:659, the InlineContentPayloads.payload column) before any byte range is applied (content_service.py ~:713). Only the verification-chunk sha256 column was ever set to EXTERNAL storage (migration 202607261700); the payload column keeps the default EXTENDED (compressed) TOAST mode, so PostgreSQL must decompress the entire value for any substr, and a chunked reader cannot be cheap today. Consequence: every read of an inline recording costs one full payload in process memory, bounded only by the inline ceiling (384 MiB default, up to the ~1 GiB hard bound); with N concurrent transcriptions that is N times the payload. eneo-qr0a lands with an honest contract (streams object-store audio; hydrates inline audio once, spools, releases) and does not change this. OWNER: eneo/object_content. DESIGN PASS REQUIRED (persistence): options include ALTER COLUMN payload SET STORAGE EXTERNAL (a rewrite of existing rows on a production table full of blobs, or applied to new rows only) plus a chunked substr reader behind the existing open_verified_read byte-range contract; or deciding by policy that recordings above a threshold must live in object storage, leaving inline reads whole and bounded. Measure before choosing: representative inline audio sizes and concurrency on the owner's deployment. Do not build a second read path; the spool owner from qr0a must simply consume whichever read the object-content owner provides.
close_reason: Both slices landed: 7cb2872a0 (EXTERNAL storage, fresh copies, background conversion, eneo-k47l) and 941d8aa87 (snapshot streaming reads, eneo-q2h0). Inline PostgreSQL object content now reads in bounded memory (a few MiB per reader regardless of object size) with the same verified spool S3 uses; the deployment guide documents rollout and the read behaviour. Not built by ruling: chunk manifests, resumable reads, a chunk-size setting, chunk-row fallback.

This bead is therefore P1 and a landing slice, not a recommendation to connect object storage. Design pass constraints set by that directive: the PostgreSQL-inline read path must stream with bounded memory as a first-class outcome; the design must cover existing rows (compressed TOAST) as well as new rows, and say whether existing rows are rewritten in batches through the existing reconciliation owner or left whole-read with the asymmetry named; the chunked reader must sit behind the existing open_verified_read byte-range contract and integrate with the existing per-chunk verification (verification_chunk_size_bytes and verification_chunk_sha256), never a second read path; the qr0a spool owner consumes it unchanged. Proof standard for the implementation: capture the SQL issued on the streaming path and assert no whole-payload select, plus a real-PostgreSQL test on a multi-chunk payload. Sequencing: design pass launches in the next free Codex slot alongside eneo-durl's; implementation after qr0a lands because the spool is its consumer.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Astra max design pass (session smxs-design) 2026-09-21 10:20: changes_required MIN 6, 'revise option 1, then proceed'. PostgreSQL's EXTERNAL substring optimization is documented and applies, but the brief understated three things. Verification: inline rows have no per-chunk hashes today (verification chunks exist for object-store objects only) and BOTH backends verify whole content before exposing response bytes, so a verified byte-range read of inline content needs new inline verification metadata and is a separate acceptance criterion. Conversion: existing compressed rows and database-to-database inserts (the move executor) must be in the plan. Read lifetime: a complete database read needs a stable snapshot and cancellation cleanup. DIRECTION the pass recommends and I adopt: the smallest memory fix reuses the canonical whole-content verification and bounded disk spooling that the object-store read already has: chunked substr reads of an EXTERNAL-stored payload stream into a bounded disk spool while hashing, the whole hash is verified at the end, then the spooled file is exposed; memory bounded by the chunk size, disk bounded by the spool, verification unchanged, no new metadata. Efficient verified ranges (serving part of an inline object without reading it all) come later with per-chunk hashes if a consumer needs them. Full findings follow in the next comment; spec to be written after the two in-flight landings; implementation after qr0a lands.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: Design findings recorded 2026-09-21 10:23 (Astra max; each claim cites source). F1 P1: per-chunk verification belongs to the object-store backend only; InlineContentPayloads has no chunk manifest and prepare_inline discards the part hashes it already captured; InlineContentStore verifies the whole payload before yielding, as S3 does. F2 P1: SET STORAGE EXTERNAL alone cannot establish the invariant: partial fetch is documented only for UNCOMPRESSED external bytea, a storage-policy change does not rewrite old values, compressed slicing can repeatedly decompress prefixes, and the database-copy writer prepare_inline_from_select copies the source datum which PostgreSQL may keep compressed; existing rows need explicit conversion and database-copy writers must produce fresh uncompressed values, preserving the byte-identity fence. F3 P1: independent slice queries race a completed move that deletes the inline payload immediately; all slices must be read inside one read-only repeatable-read snapshot, drained into the verification spool, then the transaction released before exposing the response; corruption closes the snapshot before recording failure through the placement fence; cancellation releases the connection and temp file even while opening. F4 P2: get_readable_sources still selects the whole payload and must leave the download path, while read_content_bytes intentionally batches and an integration test requires one inline query for multiple files, so metadata-slice retrieval and batch materialization stay distinct in the repository. F5 P2: at the default 256 KiB chunk a 384 MiB payload is 1536 slice queries; measure driver path, query count, application memory, PostgreSQL work and concurrent-read latency; the current inline fixture is tiny. LANDING ORDER adopted: (1) schema and writers: EXTERNAL plus fresh uncompressed values from database-copy inserts, StorageKind and deployment policy unchanged; (2) existing rows converted through the reconciler's LOCAL phase (runs without S3) in bounded resumable batches with short transactions and canonical-hash verification, not described as chunk-bounded since conversion may need whole-value memory per row; (3) read owner: repository metadata and slice operations with snapshot lifetime, reusing the existing verified-spool mechanism by extracting only the common part both stores need, whole-payload selection removed from downloads, FileDownload and the audio spool unchanged; (4) inline manifests only if range efficiency is required, which I do NOT require for the first delivery (bounded memory, not S3 range parity). Fallback if measurement rejects substring reads: chunk rows as an internal implementation of POSTGRES_INLINE. Do not build: backend branches in the audio spool, another public read API, a configurable chunk-size layer, request-time conversion, a generic migration framework, a production-wide rewrite migration. OPERATOR DECISIONS for the owner: conversion scheduling and pause/resume evidence, DDL lock timeout, disk/WAL/replica headroom, temp-file capacity, acceptable read concurrency and latency. Validate on PostgreSQL 13 (the harness) and the deployment version; inspect pg_attribute.attstorage and representative compressed values first. Spec after the in-flight landings; implementation after qr0a lands.

title: smxs slice 3: inline reads dispatch per row on the physical representation, so streaming needs no global readiness and no up-front conversion
description: Owner question 2026-09-21 19:38: must all existing inline content be converted before streaming works? With 941d8aa87 yes (one global inline_conversion_ready_at gate); the owner's dev database would grow 796 MB (11,679 of 18,389 rows compressed, 15 GB -> 16 GB) over ~2 h of background conversion, and future production installs carry gigabytes of non-flows uploads. Better owner: decide per row. get_read_metadata already reads octet_length(payload) (raw size from the TOAST header, no detoast); add pg_column_size(payload) (compressed size, header only) and dispatch: pg_column_size >= octet_length and out of line -> snapshot slice reads; otherwise -> whole-payload read exactly as today. Then: new writes stream from the first write on any deployment; old rows work unchanged and convert opportunistically or never; the global readiness gate, the drain-before-migrate rule and the WAL planning become optional operations, not prerequisites; the conversion sweep stays as a background optimization with its progress facts. Verify on PostgreSQL 13 and 16 that both size functions are header-only for compressed and uncompressed out-of-line values (no detoast in the metadata statement), that an inline (non-TOASTed, small) value is handled (whole read is fine and cheap), and that a row converted between metadata and slices inside one REPEATABLE READ snapshot still reads consistently. Keep the readiness fact for the deployment guide as an optional signal. Tests: mixed table with compressed and uncompressed rows served correctly by the two paths in one run; captured SQL proves the metadata statement performs no detoast; the benchmark module unchanged. Docs: OBJECT_CONTENT.md rollout paragraph rewritten (conversion optional). Spec + Astra validation before launch; base after eneo-iee9 lands.

OWNER DECISION still open here: an opt-in or pause control for the conversion sweep.

title: Flows at production scale: bounded human-in-the-loop waits, real retention, big audio and oversized steps (chunk, map, reduce)
description: Owner ask 2026-09-19 23:56: are flows ready for production scale; what happens to runs waiting forever on a human step; sensible defaults global or per flow; how a huge audio transcription is handled; how big steps should be handled model-agnostically (chunks/batches sized by the model), for flows and the Builder. Verified 2026-09-20 00:05 (explorers, maps in the session scratchpad): a waiting run holds no worker/lease/memory, only rows and blobs; a 14-day review expiry cancels awaiting_review/edited checkpoints via an every-minute arq cron, per-STEP override only; G1 an APPROVED-but-never-RESUMED checkpoint is excluded from expiry by design and waits forever (non-terminal, non-purgeable, invisible to health); G2 run-history purge is built and tested but has no scheduler or endpoint, the nightly cron deliberately excludes flow data, the admin retention policy never deletes; G3 edits unbounded; G4 expiry not renewed by activity; G5 default not configurable per tenant; G6 expires_at nullable. Big inputs: audio already segments (5-min chunks, serial, measured offsets) on the LiteLLM path only; no duration bound; whole-file WAV decode; transcription outside the step timeout; transcript >1 MiB fails hard; oversized model input fails closed at ModelCapacity gates and tells the user to split what the product cannot split; per_item_map is the map primitive (serial, per-item deadline re-armed, no reduce, no chunk producer); the Builder never sizes a step at proposal time; PDF extraction unbounded. Proposals A1-A5 (approve=resume; wire retention for preserve + admin purge action; tenant expiry default; activity renews expiry; NOT NULL + health age + edit bound) and B1-B6 (audio ceiling/stream/concurrency/spill; consumer-sized chunk producer; bounded reduce; mapped deadline as whole-step; Builder sizing via preview_step_execution_context; PDF bounds) in scratchpad design-production-scale.md; Astra design pass session flows-production-scale-design. Children are created after the rulings.

title: Long transcripts: review editing, corrections, speaker mapping, retry and regeneration on a file-backed transcript
description:
Deferred from eneo-6h99.4 on 2026-09-21 after its Astra spec validation (MIN 5, finding 4 and finding 5). Once a transcript above the inline cap spills to a text artifact, these owners still reject file-backed content and that rejection is PRESERVED deliberately by 6h99.4: review checkpoint editing (application/flow_run_review_checkpoint_service.py:447,:504), correction folding (flow_transcript_corrections_propagation.py:119), speaker mapping, which also rejects long renamed transcripts and synchronises the run variable by string equality (runtime/step_handlers/speaker_mapping.py:234,:284), prefix retry (application/flow_run_retry_service.py:245,:296) and transcript regeneration (flow_transcript_regeneration_service.py:252). So a five-hour recording can be transcribed and summarised but not reviewed, corrected or retried.

This needs a DESIGN PASS before any spec, because two decisions are not mechanical. (1) Artifact layout: the material reader requires FileType.TEXT and verifies the complete text's bytes and hash (step_input_resolution.py:1397,:1468), so carrying text plus segments and words needs either a second artifact or a new reader contract; today segments and words are omitted above their own thresholds. (2) Revision semantics: checkpoint originals and edit history reference payloads across immutable revisions (infrastructure/flow_run_review_checkpoint_repo.py:759,:450), so a correction must publish a NEW artifact and a new alias, never overwrite the bytes an earlier revision references, and identity must be lineage across revisions rather than a mutable pointer. Frontend loading and editing of a file-backed transcript is in scope for that design, and the 6h99.4 frontend exclusion is lifted there.

Owner rule: persistence and revision semantics are a Fable judgment moment. Depends on eneo-6h99.4.

comments.author: assistant
comments.text: RULING 2026-09-21 09:12 (Fable, after the Astra max design pass, session uwbv-design, changes_required MIN 6, one pass, no follow-up needed): DO NOT BUILD option A now; reprioritised to P3. The pass answered the whether-question decisively and I verified every fact it rests on in source. The spill fires at flow_max_inline_text_bytes, 8 MiB of transcript TEXT (main/config.py), not at any audio size. A five-hour meeting at about 150 words a minute is roughly 45,000 words, on the order of one megabyte of text even with speaker labels and timestamps, so it never spills; the five refusals stay dormant for any single recording and fire only past roughly forty hours of speech or for large-document text, where the PDF extraction ceiling is 128 MiB. My design brief conflated the 300 MiB AUDIO with the transcript, and the reviewer caught it. Reviewed minutes therefore keep the full existing inline correction path for the owner's scenario. Findings recorded as entry conditions should a product need for a corrected reusable transcript above 8 MiB ever arise: a plain-text snapshot does not compose with the correction owners, because saving corrections raises when segments are absent and regeneration renders from original segments (F1, verified); the existing result-file registration replaces an attempt's previous associations while checkpoint history still references the older artifact and export selects by latest attempt, so historical revisions strand or masquerade as current (F2, plausible, not reproduced); text downloads reject Range and correction offsets are code points, so a window editor needs a typed bounded replacement request anchored to the checkpoint revision and the immutable base file (F3, verified earlier today); a reviewer-scoped file service publishes a correction the resumed run principal cannot read (F4, verified); prefix retry is a new run and the prefix seed copies payloads without registering result files (F5); the cap owner encodes whole strings so every save costs full-file memory (F6). If it is ever built, follow the pass's landing order: retention with the first consumer, then file-backed speaker mapping with identity replacing string equality, then prefix retry independently, then bounded text editing only if source wording corrections are required, regeneration last; never a container format, mutable bytes, an unversioned latest pointer, or a whole-file browser editor. Product questions to answer first are recorded in the artifact. The real long-recording work remains qr0a and the transcription service integration, where the large object is the audio; the pending five-hour measurement (eneo-hy7c) should replace my arithmetic with a measured transcript size.

Candidate fixes, decided after the evidence: (A) runaway-output guard at the one flow completion streaming owner: abort when the streamed output repeats a window (or exceeds a per-contract output reserve the preflight already computes), typed error naming the guard, rejected text kept as evidence, so the failure costs seconds not minutes and hands to the Builder repair; (B) report never-run steps as not_run in the run summary and debug export instead of failed (one owner: flow_run_evidence_export_summary / flow_models); (C) the Builder repair for LLM_OUTPUT_TRUNCATED (S-C handoff already admits this code) should propose bounding the arrays or splitting the extraction, verify it triggers on this run. Nothing model-specific; no retry with model-specific sampling knobs.

comments.text: Astra design ruling 2026-09-21 16:08 (session long-output-design, max, changes_required MIN 7 = narrow the design). Q0: continuation in model-sized output slices is NOT a common provider contract (vLLM continue_final_message is prompt formatting, not a generation checkpoint; Azure chat has no same-message continuation; Anthropic rejects prefill on current models and forbids it with structured outputs; Ollama depends on the template); JSON can stop inside an escape, replay grows quadratically; DO NOT BUILD a continuation or cursor/chunk protocol for this incident. Safe status quo: per-call cap + deadline, reject length, never promote partial output; large results come from explicitly authored independently valid records and deterministic assembly. Two premises in my brief were wrong: flow calls are non-streaming (stream=False at step_execution_runtime.py:646) and the adapter already enforces cap = min(declared output limit, input capacity - packaged input, caller cap) (model_capacity.py:66, request_preflight.py:14); the 256-token reserve is an admission minimum, not an estimate. Q1 (slice 1, P1): truncation bypasses the existing rejected-output retention path (raises on length at :1881 before reading completion.text; other validation failures already pass rejected text into the bounded payload builder, step_output.py:26): extend the typed rejection with UTF-8-safe head/tail, byte count, sha256, sampling status, bounded by the existing evidence ceiling, captured before rejecting length, carried through the existing failed-result persistence; provider usage stays authoritative in receipts. Q2: NO streaming repetition guard now (no streaming owner; a repetition window cannot tell looping from legitimate repeated data; a probe showed a schema accepting 16,011 bytes of repeated values); conditional slice 3 only after evidence, at the adapter boundary with explicit abort semantics. Q3: no schema-to-token estimator (maxItems are permitted maxima, not expected output); no declared flow output budget exists; sectioning does not solve output expansion (one record per section must still fit one completion). Builder repair cannot impose maxItems (edit contract preserves output configuration; use requires_wider_edit). Q4 (slice 2, P2): flow_run_evidence.py becomes the one execution-status/count projection owner, not_run derived from durable markers (started_at, current_attempt_no) with terminal run state, reused by build_debug_export and flow_run_export_json; expected summary for this incident 2 completed / 1 failed / 14 not run. Order: eneo-cuty, then this bead's identity/provenance foundations, then eneo-078k (duplicate evidence + scoped consumer rewiring), then this bead's historical activation (generated types, findings screen labels, translations), then verified improvement through eneo-4x2's immutable candidate and eneo-d99. Incoming develop: 71cd89fbd73294e27bbfafbb2529674f898e20ad (image-tool localization, image references and follow-up editing, running-tool parameter expansion).

## Scope and ownership

Astra owns the integration in an isolated clean worktree. Bring the 45 incoming paths and resolve their overlap with tidy at existing owners. Regenerate the SDK from the merged OpenAPI contract. Add no independent feature or provider behavior; keep the known nested-result nullability task separate. Canonical board remains this worktree; preserve all 73 untracked files and other dirty work. Leave the running local preview unchanged.

## Steps to Reproduce

Fetch origin develop and refactor/flows-tidy-ai-builder. Verify the exact parents above and inspect the merge and incoming test changes. Current ancestry is 3 develop-only commits and 2417 tidy-only commits.

## Acceptance Criteria

Develop is an ancestor of the pushed tidy head; existing tidy commits remain ancestors. Resolve conflicts semantically, preserving image follow-up references and existing Flow file/context behavior. Run required checks and relevant affected backend, frontend and integration tests; fix failures caused by the merge without weakening contracts. Both strict typing and generated SDK drift checks pass. Record commands, outcomes, final source identity and remaining unrelated limitations. Push normally without rewriting shared history. No image publication or deployment is included in this merge request.

## Recovery

Retain both parent commits and existing local artifacts. Review the merge in isolation before fast-forwarding the canonical tidy worktree. Verify protected file hashes before and after. If origin moves, integrate its new commits instead of forcing the push.
close_reason: Develop merged and pushed; ancestry, affected behavior, strict checks and protected local files verified.

title: Flow editor: aggregate flush must recheck combined state after assistant saves
description: Found by the autosave gate (pass 3, pre-existing on tidy 9340dc05f): FlowEditor.flushSaves() awaits flushFlowSaves() then flushAssistantSaves() without rechecking the combined state. title: Builder turn stranded for the lease length when the client disconnects mid-stream
description: Observed 2026-09-06 08:00 UTC on the parent lane (:8146, tidy 6898649ad): a Vite full reload closed the browser 8 s after POST /sessions/{id}/messages was accepted. The EventSourceResponse generator was cancelled through the BaseHTTPMiddleware cancel scope; the CancelledError hit while SQLAlchemy was terminating the asyncpg connection (log: 'Exception terminating connection ... CancelledError: Cancelled via cancel scope'), so the finally in claim_ai_builder_send_turn never committed release_session_send. builder_sessions row stayed latest_turn_state=processing with lock_expires_at = accept + 900 s (ai_builder_send_lock_lease_seconds). The UI shows 'Begäran behandlas ... Vänta tills den är klar' for the whole 15 minutes, then the next claim treats the expired lock as provider_outcome_unknown. Any user who reloads or navigates during 'Eneo läser…' hits this. Owner: ai_builder_send_lease.py / ai_builder_router.py send_message event_stream. Candidate fixes to weigh: run the turn continuation detached from the response scope (task shielded from client disconnect, stream subscribes) so a reload does not cancel provider work; or at minimum release the lease under asyncio.shield with a fresh DB session on cancellation, and make the client resume the in-flight turn on reload. Evidence: parent-api docker log 08:00:47-08:00:52 UTC, session dc2127c7-3c68-4a57-bd83-f95607b47102 in eneo_ai_builder_parent.
close_reason: Landed on refactor/flows-tidy-ai-builder as 50a86976b. The send-lock cleanup now runs inside a shielded scope bounded by a module-owned 30 s cap, on a session of the lease's own, so a client disconnect clears the lock immediately instead of stranding the session for the 900 s lease. Reproductions: tests/unittests/flows/ai_builder/test_ai_builder_send_lease.py::test_client_disconnect_releases_the_send_lock (anyio cancel scope, RED on 7b314c3e8 with nothing released) and tests/integration/flows/test_ai_builder_session_api_regressions.py::test_send_message_releases_the_lock_when_the_client_disconnects (real planner + PostgreSQL, RED on base with active_request_id still held); plus test_a_release_that_never_returns_is_bounded_and_logged for the timeout path. Gate lane-reliability-wxn-gate 5 -> 6 -> 8 green. Unit tests/unittests/flows 7126 passed with the 5 pre-existing base failures; tests/integration/flows 12 failed / 4 errors = host baseline, 431 passed.

title: Harness: a saved-step edit case needs an assistant provisioning lifecycle, not a self-contained flow payload
description:
Worker impl-harness-edit-case (iteration 1, gpt-5.6-sol high) stopped BLOCKED without editing, and the spec/source mismatch it found is true: the frozen spec asked for self-contained FlowCreateRequest fixtures, but FlowStepCreateRequest requires an existing assistant_id and forbids undeclared fields including assistant instructions (backend/src/eneo/flows/api/flow_models.py:552-585); flow creation validates those ids against assistants already in the target space (flow_service.py:118-121, :491-513); assistant instructions are a separate assistant update request (flow_models.py:830-848); and flow-managed assistants can only be created after the owning flow exists (flow_assistant_router.py:78-89). So a POST /flows/ fixture cannot carry step instructions.

Resolution needed from the orchestrator before relaunching: either (a) pin stable space-scoped assistant ids for both lane stacks and reference them from the fixture, or (b) authorize a provisioning lifecycle in the harness (create flow -> create flow-managed assistants via flow_assistant_router -> configure instructions -> cleanup) and specify its fixture representation. (b) is the honest shape because the harness must also work on a fresh space.

title: Tab and segmented controls animate with transition:all on a Material curve, unlike the rest of flows
description: Measured live 2026-09-14 on the flow page. All three tab-like controls (page tabs Byggare/Historik/AI-byggaren, the Enkel/Avancerad mode toggle, the Diagram/Detaljer view toggle) compute to transition-property: all, 0.15s, cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1). That is Material's standard curve and an unnamed property list, while flows and the Builder now run on the recorded scale (--ease-smooth-out, named properties, 150/200/250 ms). The values come from the shared layout TabTrigger and the shared shadcn primitives, so they are outside the flows scope and changing them changes tabs across the whole product. Decide app-wide: name the properties instead of all, and move the curve onto the recorded easing. Tab panels themselves switch instantly, which is correct for a frequent navigation action; the Builder's own screen entrance is the only content motion and should stay a screen-state animation, not become a tab effect.

title: Citation tracking for JSON completion output (section records and summarize folds carry no citations today)
description: Found 2026-09-21 10:48 when the summarize-fold worker blocked correctly: citation capability is text-only in three owners: flow_capability_manifest.py:749 defines it as text-only, flow_validators.py:724 rejects citation mode for non-text output, and step_execution_runtime.py:1029 disables tracking for JSON output. Consequence: section-processing records (JSON) and therefore summarize folds carry no citations, so a grounded material summarised over sections loses its source identities downstream. The worker's proposed owner-level change, recorded for a design pass: extend the existing inline_inref_sidecar capability to JSON completion output, align validation and runtime selection, and extract and strip references within JSON string values while preserving the authored schema, with a grounded-input execution regression rather than injected ids. Needs a design pass before a spec; not part of eneo-6h99.5, whose contract now states that records inherit citations when parents carry any and carry none otherwise.

title: Flows DOCX templates: optional number, date and select bindings render empty, not an error
description: Found by flow-discovery (2026-09-23) while fixing omitted optional form fields (05ef0994d): optional number, date and select fields resolve to None, and render_docx_template treats None as an error, so a whole-expression DOCX binding of such a field fails whether the field is left out or sent empty. List and multiselect fields bound as a whole expression are refused as structured data. Text fields are fixed by 05ef0994d (the control is removed). Behaviour wanted: an empty optional value removes or empties the control like an empty text field, at the one DOCX block writer (see memory docx-content-control-templates). Tests: each optional type left out and sent empty renders a document.

title: Suggestion handoff message is Swedish-only and its order is built twice
description:
Found by the Codex commit gate (session review-suggestions-gate, iteration 22, 2026-09-06) while gating the batch handoff UI.

The server writes the canonical investigation message and ignores what the client sent (SendMessageRequest.canonical() -> investigation_message() in ai_builder_flow_review.py). Two consequences:

1. investigation_message() renders hard-coded Swedish regardless of the turn's ui_language, so an English user types nothing, sees an English optimistic message from the client, and after a refresh the persisted conversation shows Swedish.

2. The display text is constructed twice: the client builds a preview in flowReviewSuggestions.investigationMessage() in the response order and the active locale, while the server sorts and deduplicates the foci canonically before rendering. For a batch the two can disagree in item order, so the optimistic message and the persisted one differ.

Codex's smallest correction: have the server render the requested UI language and align ordering, or return the canonical display message so the client stops duplicating its construction. The second is the better shape - one owner for the sentence - but it changes the send response, so it wants its own slice.

Not urgent: the product is Swedish-first and the mismatch is cosmetic, but an English tenant sees a Swedish sentence in their own conversation.
close_reason: Fixed on tidy by 02dcc63eb (a parallel session): the screen and the server now compose the same sentence from the same fixed parts in the request's UI language, over one canonical deduplicated and ordered set of suggestions, so the optimistic text, the fingerprint and the retained message agree. Nothing left to do.

title: Long transcription jobs finish, fail honestly and wait when Vemsa is busy
description:
Problem (verified 2026-09-20 against tidy d617aae72 and vemsa main): Eneo admits audio up to FLOW_AUDIO_MAX_DURATION_SECONDS=14400 (4 h) but every remote transcription job must submit, wait in Vemsa's queue, transcribe and diarize inside FLOW_STEP_BUDGET_SECONDS=3600: remote_transcription.py wait_for_result/_poll_until_result cancel the job service-side when the step deadline expires. A legitimate multi-hour recording is cancelled after an hour of GPU work and reported as a step timeout. Two smaller contract holes on the same path: (1) every Vemsa 'failed' status maps to provider_rejected_request / retryable=false (_poll_until_result), although Vemsa fails jobs for out-of-memory after VEMSA_OOM_MAX_ATTEMPTS, whisper timeouts and provider outages, and its JobStatusResponse.error text is never read; (2) a 429 at submit (queue full 100, or the per-client cap 10, api/jobs.py:63-90) fails the step at once with provider_rate_limited, so a mapped flow over many recordings fails when Vemsa is merely busy.

Owner: backend/src/eneo/flows/runtime/remote_transcription.py (RemoteTranscriptionClient / RemoteFlowTranscriber) with step_deadline.py as the budget owner. Reuse: audio_seconds is already measured before submit (measure_duration); the deadline scope already distinguishes provider work in flight; the PDF slice's 'busy: wait and retry' semantics (flow_upload_pdf_extraction_busy).

Deliverable (one behaviour slice, no new settings): (a) a remote job waits under the run's invocation ceiling (task_execution_timeout_seconds remaining), not the fixed step budget, because the work is provider-side, cancellable and progress-reported (stage, queue_position); the step budget keeps bounding local phases. Alternative if the design pass prefers evidence-based waiting: Vemsa exposes updated_at on the status response and Eneo waits while the job stays alive. Decide in a one-pass design brief; the owner ruling is one default that just works for a 4 h file. (b) Vemsa's failure kind reaches the flow run error: read the status 'error' (and the closed failure_kind once the Vemsa bead lands) and map capacity/provider failures to retryable provider_error, validation failures to provider_rejected_request; the FlowRunErrorDetails phase stays TRANSCRIPTION. (c) submit 429 waits and retries on the poll interval within the deadline (Retry-After when present), mirroring the busy-extractor rule; cancel semantics unchanged.

Non-goals: webhooks instead of polling (needs an inbound endpoint, auth and a task wake-up; polling under the deadline is the simpler robust path, decided not missed); chunked transcription; a duration-derived budget factor (a magic constant).

Acceptance: a fake service that completes after longer than the step budget but inside the run ceiling yields a transcript; a service 'failed' with an OOM/capacity error yields a retryable provider_error carrying the service reason; a 429 followed by 202 submits once the queue admits; existing cancellation tests unchanged. Validation: tests/unittests/flows (remote transcription tests), tests/unit/flows, OpenAPI contract file if a public field changes; bare pyright 0; the flows integration suite before landing. Depends on eneo-ls78 for the ceiling wording in docs; the Vemsa-side bead supplies failure_kind.

title: Review session permission does not survive conversation compaction
description:
Found by the Codex commit gate (session review-suggestions-gate, pass 15, 2026-09-06) on feature/ai-builder-review-suggestions.

The AI Builder review permission (flows_ai_builder_review / FlowApiAction.BUILDER_REVIEW) is decided per turn from a retained user message that names a review: conversation_acts_on_a_review() in ai_builder_conversation_metadata.py, used at both decision points in ai_builder_router.send_message. Conversation compaction keeps required units, preferred schema sources and a bounded tail (ai_builder_conversation_compaction.py, _required_message_indices), and review references are not among the required owners. A review outlives the turn that opened it by design, so a long enough review conversation loses its only marker and subsequent turns fall back to ordinary Builder authorization while still being a review-derived session.

This is pre-existing: before the 2026-09-06 slice the same decision was made from latest_user_review_context(), which has the same dependency on a retained message. The slice neither caused nor worsened it.

Do NOT fix by pinning the review message in _required_message_indices: test_the_floor_survives_the_real_compactor_dropping_the_review_message asserts that compaction drops the review message deliberately, and that the evidence floor survives because every accepted turn re-writes EVIDENCE_FLOOR_METADATA_KEY into the bounded tail. That is the established pattern for a fact that must outlive compaction, and it is the model to follow: carry a durable 'this session acts on a review' marker on every accepted turn's metadata the same way the floor is carried. Note that the floor itself is not a substitute, because metadata_for_user_message only writes it when it is non-zero, so a review over level-0 evidence writes none.

Acceptance: a review session compacted past its opening turn still requires BUILDER_REVIEW on the next turn, with a test that drives the real compactor.
close_reason: Landed on tidy 8640fa7e4: the review permission survives count and byte compaction via the per-turn marker

title: After the Builder creates a flow you land on 'Grundinställningar', not on the steps you just approved
description: Found live 2026-09-14 on a from-scratch create journey. After approving a 4-step plan and confirming 'Skapa flödet', the app opens the new flow's editor at stage 1 'Grundinställningar' (aria-current=step), which asks for name and description, both of which the Builder just filled in. The user has spent the whole journey reviewing steps and is dropped on the one stage that has nothing to do with them; the steps they approved are two stages away under 'Bearbetningssteg'. Decide the right landing after an AI create (the steps stage, or a short 'what happens now' with Publicera as the single next action) and make focus land on it.
